entry.title: One-bit-per-gate distributed garbling and constant-round malicious-secure MPC
entry.summary: One-Bit-per-Gate Distributed Garbling and Constant-Round Malicious MPC IACR ePrint · Nov 26, 2026This paper presents a distributed garbling protocol in which several mutually distrustful parties jointly generate a garbled circuit that keeps the privacy and authenticity of a single trusted garbler as long as one party is honest. Under Ring-LWE and constant-locality PRG assumptions, each garbler communicates an amortized one bit per gate. The protocol uses constant rounds and remains secure against a malicious adversary corrupting all but one garbler. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a distributed garbling protocol with about one bit per gate per garbler, constant rounds, and malicious security under Ring-LWE and constant-locality PRG assumptions.

entry.title: DEEP Revisited: Proximity Gaps Up to List-Decoding Radius Using Out-of-Domain Samples
entry.summary: DEEP Revisited: Proximity Gaps up to List-Decoding Radius via Out-of-Domain Samples IACR ePrint · Nov 26, 2026This paper revisits the use of out-of-domain samples for proximity gaps, a technique first introduced in DEEP-FRI. Over sufficiently large fields, multiple such samples give proximity-gap guarantees for linear codes at any list-decodable radius below the minimum distance. For general linear codes, the guarantee extends from the one-and-a-half Johnson bound to the full Johnson bound using a constant number of samples. For Reed-Solomon codes, the bounds hold beyond the Johnson radius even when the list size is much larger than 2^λ. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors extend out-of-domain sample proximity gaps from the one-and-a-half Johnson bound to the full Johnson bound, giving proofs and error and sample-count analyses relevant to hash-based SNARK s

entry.title: A Faster Provable Algorithm for Random Modular Subset Sum
entry.summary: Faster Provable Algorithm For Random Modular Subset Sum IACR ePrint · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies the random modular subset sum problem, where coefficients are drawn uniformly modulo Q and the target is the inner product with a hidden binary vector. It focuses on the balanced density-one case with Q=2^n and Hamming weight n/2. The authors present a classical randomized algorithm that, for sufficiently large n, finds a solution with overwhelming probability using at most 2^0.2614n bit operations and 2^0.2373n bits of space, without heuristic assumptions. This improves on the previously reported best classical time bound of 2^0.283n. ★★★★ Notable: The authors improve the classical time bound for balanced density-one random modular subset sum from 2^0.283n to 2^0.2614n, without heuristic assumptions, also giving a space bound.

entry.title: Classical key agreement with near-quadratic quantum security
entry.summary: Classical Key Agreement with Near-Quadratic Quantum Security IACR ePrint · Nov 26, 2026The paper presents two classical key-establishment protocols in the random oracle query model: a two-message protocol and a three-message protocol with perfect agreement. Honest parties make about Õ(N) classical oracle queries, while any quantum eavesdropper with constant success probability needs Õ(N²) quantum queries to recover the key. The result is tight up to logarithmic factors, since the quadratic classical attack of Barak and Mahmoody also applies in this setting. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present two classical key agreement protocols where honest parties use near-linear queries while quantum eavesdroppers need near-quadratic queries, tight up to logarithmic factors.

entry.title: NP-completeness of worst-case (2,1) quasi-cyclic syndrome decoding
entry.summary: On the NP-Completeness of Worst-Case (2,1)-Quasi-Cyclic Syndrome Decoding IACR ePrint · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies the worst-case (2,1) quasi-cyclic syndrome decoding problem over the ring F2[X]/(X^n-1), asking whether polynomials x and y exist with x+hy=s and equal block weights w. The authors prove the problem is NP-complete in the low-weight regime w<√n via a polynomial-time reduction from 3-Dimensional Matching. The same reduction also covers a relaxed variant requiring only weights at most w. The result is further extended to prime block lengths and general fixed (a,b)-QCSD instances. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report NP-completeness of worst-case (2,1)-QCSD via a polynomial reduction from 3DM, extending to prime lengths and general (a,b) instances.

entry.title: Fault attacks that recover secret keys from three post-quantum signature schemes
entry.summary: Faulting the Proof: Key Recovery Attacks on MQOM, SDitH and FAEST IACR ePrint · Nov 26, 2026This paper examines how well the MQOM, SDitH and FAEST signature schemes resist faults during computation of their proof of key knowledge. The authors exploit a value that is omitted from signatures but still bound through a hash, using it to test key guesses from faulty signatures. Clock-glitch experiments on an STM32F405 microcontroller recover the full secret key of all three schemes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show an omitted value bound by a hash enables fault-based key guessing, correcting prior MQOM analysis; they report full key recovery on all three schemes via clock glitches on an STM32F40

entry.title: Recovering the full structure of linearized Reed–Solomon codes from a generator matrix
entry.summary: Full Structure Recovery of Linearized Reed–Solomon Codes IACR ePrint · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies linearized Reed–Solomon (LRS) codes, which are considered for post-quantum code-based cryptography. The authors present a polynomial-time procedure that recovers the full structure of an LRS code using only an arbitrary generator matrix. The results show that LRS codes, like Hamming and rank-metric codes, cannot be used as they are for McEliece-like encryption. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a polynomial-time full structure recovery of LRS codes from an arbitrary generator matrix, combining Overbeck-type attacks with shortening, implying LRS codes are unsuitable for Mc

entry.title: Parity leakage and sparse-mask sampling in distorted McEliece pseudorandom codes
entry.summary: Parity Leakage and Sparse-Mask Sampling in Distorted-McEliece Pseudorandom Codes IACR ePrint · Nov 27, 2026The paper examines the binary public-key pseudorandom codes proposed by Dyseryn, Francati and Venturi, showing that with the full support their public key can be distinguished from a uniform matrix by computing parities, which refutes their Distorted McEliece Public Key assumption. It characterises which supports leak through vanishing power sums and analyses how sparse distortions act on dual codewords. It also studies sampling methods for the mask, and states that the ciphertext-level assumption is not refuted. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show the DFV key assumption fails for full support via parity leakage, characterize support restrictions, and analyse mask sampling methods.

entry.title: Impossibility Results for Perfect Additive Randomized Encodings
entry.summary: On Perfect Additive Randomized Encodings IACR ePrint · Nov 27, 2026This paper studies Additive Randomized Encodings (AREs), which encode each input locally so that the function output can be decoded from the sum of the encodings while revealing nothing else about the inputs. The authors show that no ARE can achieve both perfect security and perfect correctness for OR over any finite Abelian group, and likewise for XOR over Z_p with prime p>2 under a rationality assumption. They also partially rule out perfectly correct AREs for OR with imperfect security under natural restrictions, and rule out perfectly secure AREs with nontrivial correctness error over histograms, which extends to protocols in the shuffle model. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove nonexistence of perfect AREs for OR over finite Abelian groups and XOR over Z_p, with partial negative results for perfectly correct AREs.

entry.title: Near-n-bit preimage and second-preimage security of the JH hash mode
entry.summary: Near-n-Bit Preimage and Second-Preimage Security of the JH Mode IACR ePrint · Nov 27, 2026This paper revisits the JH hash mode in the ideal-permutation model, where earlier direct bounds on preimage and second-preimage resistance were only at the birthday scale. Using Menger's theorem and a potential function, the authors derive bounds that give negligible advantage for messages up to 2^64 bits within about 2^(n-2√(2n)-O(log n)) queries. For JH-512, the certificates keep preimage success below 1/2 up to 2^431 queries and second-preimage up to 2^416. A Lean 4 formalization of the proofs is included. ★★★★ Notable: In the ideal-permutation model, the authors use Menger's theorem and a potential to improve JH preimage and second-preimage bounds from birthday scale, with Lean 4 proofs.

entry.title: Extending Arithmetic Masking Security to All Finite Cyclic Groups via Fourier Analysis
entry.summary: Extending the Security of Arithmetic Masking to All Finite Cyclic Groups via Fourier Analysis IACR ePrint · Nov 27, 2026This paper studies a secret-sharing scheme in which a secret in the integers modulo N is split into k shares, and bounds how far the joint distribution of the shares' Hamming weights is from the distribution obtained when the secret is uniform. The authors prove that for every N≥2 and fixed k≥3, this total variation distance is O(n^(-k/2+5/4)) uniformly over all secrets, where n is the ceiling of log2 N. The proof uses Fourier analysis on the Boolean cube and a decomposition of the range into intervals with power-of-two lengths. The result removes the earlier requirement that the modulus be close to a power of two, while keeping the exponent of the general bound by Biswas et al. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend arithmetic masking security bounds from near-power-of-two moduli to all finite cyclic groups via Fourier analysis on the Boolean cube.

entry.title: Exact post-quantum security analysis of Ascon authenticated encryption under nonce misuse
entry.summary: Exact Post-Quantum Security Analysis of Ascon Authenticated Encryption under Nonce Misuse IACR ePrint · Nov 27, 2026This paper studies the post-quantum security of Ascon AEAD, a lightweight authenticated encryption algorithm standardized by NIST as SP 800-232, when nonces are reused. Using the quantum random permutation model, the authors prove confidentiality and authenticity security up to min{2^(κ/2), 2^(c/3)} queries, improving the key-length dependence of a previous bound from 2^(κ/3). They also construct quantum attacks based on classical nonce-misuse attacks, showing that the bounds are tight in the exponent. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a new decomposition of Ascon AEAD, improve the key-length dependence of a prior bound, and report matching quantum attacks showing tight bounds.

entry.title: "Adams Bridge is Falling Down": New Chosen-Ciphertext Side-Channel Attack on a Post-Quantum Crypto Accelerator
entry.summary: Adams Bridge is Falling Down: A New Chosen Ciphertext Side-Channel Attack on the PQC Accelerator IACR ePrint · Nov 25, 2026This paper reports new vulnerabilities in the Adams Bridge hardware accelerator, which implements ML-KEM and ML-DSA and serves as the post-quantum engine of Caliptra 2.1. The authors present the first practical key recovery attack on the released v2.0.3 ML-KEM implementation with all countermeasures enabled. They also propose a non-profiled chosen-ciphertext attack that recovers the full ML-KEM-1024 secret key using 18,580 traces in 49.5 minutes, reducing traces by at least 29.2% compared with their profiled attack. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a new non-profiled chosen-ciphertext side-channel attack, reporting the first practical key recovery on Adams Bridge ML-KEM with all countermeasures enabled.

entry.title: Faster Key Generation and UC Security Without Global Abort for Lindell's Two-Party ECDSA
entry.summary: Improving Lindell's Two-Party ECDSA: Faster Key Generation and UC Security Without Global Abort IACR ePrint · Nov 25, 2026This paper improves the two-party ECDSA signing protocol by Lindell (CRYPTO '17), addressing its slow key generation and its reliance on a global abort mechanism. The authors build a faster zero-knowledge proof for the Paillier-EC discrete logarithm relation using Bulletproofs and a commitment bridge linking Paillier ciphertexts to elliptic-curve Pedersen commitments. They claim UC security against malicious adversaries without global abort, with key generation time estimated to be about four times faster and small signing overhead. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use Bulletproofs-based commitment bridges to speed up PDL proofs and remove global abort for UC security. They report production implementation performance, relevant to blockchain two-part

entry.title: Nearly Optimal Lower Bounds for Pairing-Based Succinct Non-Interactive Arguments
entry.summary: (Almost) Tight Bounds for Pairing-Based SNARGs IACR ePrint · Nov 25, 2026This paper constructs a publicly verifiable succinct non-interactive argument (SNARG) for NP in the asymmetric bilinear generic group and random oracle models. At λ bits of security, a proof consists of one G1 element plus λ+o(λ) additional bits. Assuming exponentially secure pseudorandom generators and natural restrictions on setup and verification, the authors show the additional bit string cannot have length o(λ). They also present a variant of the KZG polynomial commitment scheme that saves one pairing during verification compared with standard KZG. ★★★★ Notable: The authors construct a pairing-based SNARG with near-tight proof-length bounds and a KZG variant saving one pairing.

entry.title: Constant-size identity-based linkable ring signatures using standard assumptions
entry.summary: Constant-Size Identity-Based Linkable Ring Signatures from Standard Assumptions IACR ePrint · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes an identity-based linkable ring signature scheme whose signatures have constant size and whose security is proven in the standard model under standard assumptions. Earlier schemes of this kind were proven secure only in the random oracle model, and those with constant-size signatures also relied on non-standard assumptions. The construction is built from a constant-size hierarchical identity-based encryption scheme, adapted to a matrix-based dual-system framework. The authors prove unforgeability, linkability, and non-slanderability under the Matrix Decisional Diffie-Hellman assumption. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a constant-size identity-based linkable ring signature in the standard model, with security proven under the MDDH assumption.

entry.title: Beyond the Input-Length Barrier: How Many AND and OT Calls Secure Two-Party Computation Needs
entry.summary: Beyond the Input-Length Barrier: AND and OT Complexity of Two-Party Computation IACR ePrint · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how many calls to AND or Oblivious Transfer (OT) are needed to securely compute a given function between two parties. The authors prove that Inner Product, equality, and Hamming proximity require about 1.29n AND calls, and that almost every Boolean function on two n-bit inputs requires about 1.26n OT calls. They also give a perfectly secure randomized protocol for Inner Product using about 1.71n AND calls. Finally, they show randomized protocols can be derandomized in parallel without increasing the number of AND calls. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give explicit AND and OT call lower bounds beyond input length, plus an improved randomized AND protocol for Inner Product.

entry.title: When Verification Leaks: Fixing Verifiable PIR That Reveals Queries
entry.summary: When Verification Leaks: Breaking and Repairing Verifiable PIR with Small Client Storage IACR ePrint · Nov 25, 2026Verifiable private information retrieval (vPIR) lets a client privately fetch a database entry and check the server's answer. A 2026 IEEE S&P scheme reduces client storage by delegating hint computations to the server with homomorphic encryption, claiming that accepting or rejecting responses leaks nothing about the query. This paper refutes that claim with two selective-failure attacks by a malicious server. It then repairs the scheme by requiring the server to prove that returned ciphertexts are correct before decryption, preserving query privacy and answer correctness without large client storage. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a selective-failure attack on a small-storage vPIR scheme and a proof-based repair that removes the leak.

entry.title: Quorus 2.0: A Practical, Scalable Threshold Signature Scheme for the NIST-Standardized ML-DSA
entry.summary: Quorus 2.0: Practical and Scalable Threshold Signature Scheme for NIST-Standardized ML-DSA IACR ePrint · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents a threshold signature scheme for ML-DSA, the post-quantum signature algorithm standardized by NIST as FIPS 204, allowing a group of signers, none of whom holds the full key, to jointly produce signatures that pass the unmodified standard verification. The authors note limitations of prior approaches, including party-count limits, many online rounds, and reliance on added noise or extra assumptions. They prove that transcripts of rejected signing attempts can be simulated statistically without noise or additional assumptions. Building on this, they construct an efficient protocol using only arithmetic modulo ML-DSA's native modulus q. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove rejected ML-DSA transcripts can be simulated statistically without noise or extra assumptions, and build a threshold scheme using only arithmetic modulo q that scales to any n.

entry.title: Forging Encrypted Checksums in Verifiable FHE: A Cryptanalysis of DataSeal
entry.summary: Forging Encrypted Linear Checksums in Verifiable FHE: A Cryptanalysis of DataSeal IACR ePrint · Nov 25, 2026This paper examines DataSeal (IEEE S&P 2025), a scheme that gives a fully homomorphic encryption evaluator encrypted secret linear checksums. It shows attacks that let an incorrect output pass verification, including forgeries against each of its two matrix checks. The authors also analyze a repair that adds independent checksum rows and run SEAL/BGV experiments to test the feasibility of the attacks and selected countermeasures. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors present forgeries against DataSeal's linear checksums and analyze multi-row repairs; they report executing attacks on SEAL/BGV and changing MNIST predictions.

entry.title: MechCrypto: AI-assisted cryptanalysis of first-round NGCC candidate algorithms
entry.summary: MechCrypto: Agent-Assisted Cryptanalysis of the First-Round NGCC Candidates IACR ePrint · Nov 26, 2026This paper presents MechCrypto, a cryptanalysis research agent built on a persistent graph-structured framework, combining task contracts, cross-artifact provenance, on-demand cryptographic knowledge packs, and an independent verification gate. The authors blindly evaluated it on all 119 first-round candidates of the NGCC program, covering signatures, key encapsulation, key exchange, and hash functions, without access to existing attack reports. The campaign produced 115 comparable principal results, including 23 Critical findings. The authors report higher severity ratings than the public results on several candidates. ★★★★ Notable: The authors apply a persistent graph-structured agent to cryptanalysis with an independent verification gate; the abstract reports 115 principal results across 119 NGCC candidates, 23 rated Critical.

entry.title: Computational Bernoulli Smoothing and Worst-Case Errors in LPN Reductions
entry.summary: Computational Bernoulli Smoothing and Worst-Case Errors in LPN Reductions IACR ePrint · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies Learning Parity with Noise (LPN), a central problem in post-quantum cryptography, and improves a worst-case hardness reduction by Aggarwal et al. (TCC 2026) for the low-noise regime. The authors remove two restrictions of that result: Bernoulli error for the decoding alternative and fixed-weight noise for the dual distinguishing alternative. Their main tool is a computational Bernoulli perturbation bound for finite groups, which states that if a perturbed distribution is ε-pseudorandom, the original is ε/(1-2β)-pseudorandom, and this bound is shown to be tight. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a computational Bernoulli perturbation bound for finite groups, removing prior noise-distribution restrictions in LPN reductions, with a tight bound.

entry.title: Breaking the Curse of Dimensionality: Fuzzy PSI Without Extra Overhead
entry.summary: Breaking the Curse of Dimensionality: Fuzzy PSI without O((log δ)^d) Overhead IACR ePrint · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents a fuzzy private set intersection (FPSI) protocol for L∞ distance, which lets a receiver learn which sender items lie within a threshold δ of its own items without revealing other information. The protocol uses only oblivious transfer and symmetric-key operations and achieves optimal O(d log δ) fuzzy matching complexity without an extra O((log δ)^d) factor. Experiments show it outperforms state-of-the-art FPSI protocols under all tested parameters, with 1.2 to 174 times faster running time and 1.5 to 97.4 times lower communication cost. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a new ssPIT protocol that yields O(d log δ) fuzzy matching without an extra exponential factor, reporting 1.2–174× speedup and 1.5–97.4× communication reduction over prior FPSI.

entry.title: Remote fault attack on post-quantum signatures using statistical ineffective fault analysis
entry.summary: Remote Fault Attacks on PIOP-based Post-Quantum Digital Signatures using Statistical Ineffective Fault Analysis IACR ePrint · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents a remote fault attack against post-quantum digital signature schemes MQOM, FAEST and SDitH, which are based on Polynomial Interactive Oracle Proof (PIOP) protocols. The attack targets the underlying polynomials to recover the secret key and uses Statistical Ineffective Fault Analysis, demonstrated end-to-end with Rowhammer. The authors claim it is the first remote attack on such a scheme that can bypass fault detection countermeasures. The paper also describes a new method to bypass address space layout randomisation and proposes countermeasures. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors apply SIFA to PIOP signatures and report an end-to-end remote Rowhammer attack recovering keys while bypassing fault detection.

entry.title: A deterministic subexponential-time algorithm for solving the discrete logarithm problem
entry.summary: A Deterministic Subexponential-time Algorithm for the Discrete Logarithm Problem IACR ePrint · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents a deterministic algorithm for the discrete logarithm problem on prime-order elliptic curves over prime fields and in the multiplicative group of prime fields. Under the assumption stated by the authors, it runs in worst-case time p^{o(1)} and uses no random bits. The proof combines a deterministic construction of small affine-interval factor bases with a terminal-preserving partial contraction procedure. ★★★★ Notable: The authors claim a deterministic subexponential discrete logarithm algorithm under an assumed external construction, a striking result whose reliance on that assumption is not checkable from the abst

entry.title: EpochPIR: A Single-Server Private Retrieval Scheme with Low Communication and Near-Optimal Speed
entry.summary: EpochPIR: Low Amortized Communication PIR at Near-Optimal Throughput IACR ePrint · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents EpochPIR, a single-server private information retrieval scheme that tries to combine low communication with high server throughput. It reuses negacyclic rotations of one ring-LWE secret across several queries, letting the server precompute the needed hint products in batches, and uses a two-stage design with a SimplePIR-based column selector and an FHE row selector. Retrieving a 256-byte entry from an 8 GB database requires 74 KB of communication per query at 10.7 GB/s single-core throughput, about 77% of SimplePIR's. A communication-optimized variant uses 26 KB per query. ★★★★ Notable: The authors reuse negacyclic rotations of one RLWE secret across queries and batch hint products via 2D NTT, reporting results on an 8 GB database against SimplePIR, Spiral and ReinsPIRe.

entry.title: Neural network decoders that account for qubit loss in quantum error correction
entry.summary: Neural Network Decoders For Qubit Loss arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper presents a loss-aware convolutional neural network (CNN) decoder framework and a new sampler, slim, for training and simulating circuits with Pauli and loss errors. On the surface code, the decoder matches the accuracy of computationally expensive most-likely error (MLE) decoders at much lower latency. For the [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle (Gross) code, at physical error rates below 1%, the authors observe a logical error rate more than 10^3 times lower under a pure loss model than under a pure Pauli model at the same physical error rate, with enhanced sub-threshold scaling. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a loss-aware CNN decoder and sampler slim, matching MLE accuracy on the surface code at lower latency and reporting over 10^3-fold lower logical error rates on the [[144,12,12]] Gr

entry.title: Exact limit on how many neighbors can steer a multimode Gaussian node
entry.summary: Exact monogamy of steering and remote Wigner negativity for multimode Gaussian nodes arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper studies how many neighbors can steer a quantum optical node with k modes when the Gaussian states are linked through a network. For Gaussian measurements, it shows the exact limit is 2k-1, regardless of squeezing, amplification or noise. The same number also bounds how many neighbors can be made Wigner negative by a heralded non-Gaussian operation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove that Gaussian multimode nodes can be steered by exactly 2k-1 neighbors and extend the same count to remote Wigner negativity.

entry.title: Bound magic states in multi-qubit systems
entry.summary: Bound magic in multi-qubit systems arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proves that some multi-qubit nonstabilizer states cannot yield pure magic, even with arbitrarily many copies and rounds of stabilizer operations. The authors introduce a PPT-like criterion for magic that is closed under tensor products and stabilizer operations and reduces to the stabilizer polytope for one and two qubits. Using this criterion, they prove the existence of multi-qubit bound magic and explicitly construct such states for three or more qubits. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove multi-qubit bound magic exists, introduce a PPT-like criterion for magic, and give explicit constructions for n≥3 qubits.

entry.title: Which quantum-state transformations are allowed under a general class of free operations in texture resource theory
entry.summary: State convertibility in quantum-state texture from a general form of free operations arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper studies which transformations between quantum states are permitted in the quantum-state texture resource theory. It fully characterizes free operations in arbitrary finite dimension and derives an exact deterministic conversion criterion for mixed states in higher dimensions. The criterion reduces to a search problem that can be solved with semidefinite programming. The characterization can also be used to study probabilistic and assisted manipulation of quantum-state texture. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give an exact deterministic conversion criterion for mixed states in arbitrary finite dimension via a decomposition of free operations into filter and CP map, reducible to SDP.

entry.title: Monotonic measures of asymmetry and how robust the quantum Mpemba effect is
entry.summary: Monotonic probes of asymmetry and robustness of the quantum Mpemba effect arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies a family of asymmetry measures based on sandwiched Rényi divergences, which are monotonic under symmetry-preserving quantum channels. The authors develop a two-parameter replica approach to compute these quantities from charged moments and show a correspondence with conventional Rényi asymmetries under the inversion of the Rényi index. For quenches from tilted ferromagnetic states, they find that the quantum Mpemba effect occurs throughout the entire family of these monotones. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build sandwiched Rényi asymmetry monotones, establish an α↔1/α correspondence with conventional Rényi asymmetries, and test quantum Mpemba robustness in quenches.

entry.title: How the copies needed to certify typical pure quantum states change sharply
entry.summary: Sharp Transitions of Copy Complexity in Local Certification of Typical Pure States arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper determines how many copies of an n-qudit quantum state are needed to certify it using tensor-product measurements. The optimal number scales as Θ(n^r), where the exponent r is a piecewise constant function of g=(a-b)/(1-b), and the authors give an exact algorithm for its breakpoints. The result holds for families of pure target states whose Haar measure tends to one as n grows. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report exact copy-complexity exponents with piecewise-constant dependence on g, matching upper and lower bounds under tensor-product measurements.

entry.title: Magic Moments: Certifying Quantum Nonstabilizer Resources from Few Copies
entry.summary: Magic Moments: An Operational Approach of Certifying Nonstabilizerness from Few Copies arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes a criterion that certifies magic, the nonstabilizerness resource needed for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation, using a few moments of the discrete Wigner function rather than full reconstruction. For pure states of any number of qudits, the criterion is necessary and sufficient, while for mixed states the authors build a hierarchy of higher-moment conditions reaching the exact negativity threshold. Each moment is measurable as a two-outcome observable's expectation on a few state copies, using a constant-depth Clifford circuit with a round count independent of qudit number. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a moment-based magic certification criterion, necessary and sufficient for pure states and reaching the exact negativity threshold for mixed states via higher-moment hierarchies.

entry.title: Planckian lower bound on thermalization time for strongly coupled open quantum systems
entry.summary: Planckian bounds on thermalization times of strongly coupled open quantum systems arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper examines whether the thermalization time of strongly coupled open quantum systems, whose equilibrium state is the mean-force Gibbs state, is bounded by the Planckian time scale ħ/k_B T. By requiring the same process to thermalize a family of nearby system Hamiltonians, it derives a lower bound independent of specific system-bath dynamics. The bound depends only on the distinguishability of the mean-force Gibbs states and can be computed from equilibrium properties. It is characterized in exactly solvable fermionic models, the spin-boson model, and a spin coupled to a two-dimensional Heisenberg antiferromagnet. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive a system-bath-independent Planckian lower bound on thermalization time from equilibrium quantities, characterized across several strong-coupling models.

entry.title: A proof of error bounds for a transverse spin-gradient approximation in noncollinear spin density theory
entry.summary: The transverse spin-gradient approximation in noncollinear spin density functional theory arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proves a quantitative error bound for a fixed-axis variant of the transverse spin-gradient approximation in noncollinear spin density functional theory. It uses a spin-spiral wave as the local reference, writing the energy as an integral depending on the total density, the magnetization and its first derivatives. When the relevant length scale is N^{1/3}, the error is O(N^{5/6}) for an energy of order N. Setting the spiral phase to zero recovers the noncollinear local spin density approximation for arbitrary magnetization directions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a quantitative error bound for a fixed-axis transverse spin-gradient approximation using spin-spiral waves as local reference in noncollinear DFT.

entry.title: "Gaussian Is All You Need": Renyi Optimizers and Optical Channel Simulation
entry.summary: Gaussian Is All You Need: Renyi Optimizers and Optical Channel Simulation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how much entanglement is needed to prepare an entangled state and how fidelity falls when less is available. The authors prove that for any finite-energy multimode bosonic Gaussian state, the entanglement cost and Renyi entanglement of formation of orders above one are additive and attained by a Gaussian pure-state decomposition. Consequently, the closest separable state in fidelity to a Gaussian state is Gaussian, and the strong converse exponent of entanglement dilution can be computed exactly. For channels, pure Gaussian inputs minimize output Renyi entropies of multimode Gaussian channels, and the optimal fidelity of simulating pure-loss and quantum-limited amplifier channels with finite entanglement is obtained. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove additivity of Rényi entanglement measures for multimode Gaussian states and that pure Gaussian inputs minimize output Rényi entropies of Gaussian channels.

entry.title: A complexity result showing tokenisation is not in APX
entry.summary: Tokenisation is not in APX arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper proves that, unless P=NP, no polynomial-time algorithm can find a tokeniser whose objective is within any constant factor of the optimum, so tokenisation is not in the APX class. The proof covers direct and bottom-up tokenisation, both compression and unigram log-likelihood objectives, and binary or larger alphabets. It further shows that direct tokenisation is APX-hard even over unary alphabets, so no polynomial-time approximation scheme exists. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove tokenisation admits no constant-factor polynomial-time approximation unless P=NP, and show APX-hardness for direct tokenisation.

entry.title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer: a Transformer that reuses layers in loops more efficiently
entry.summary: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes the Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT), which reuses shared layers across loops and selectively reads keys and values as memory between loops to balance expressivity and efficiency. It also introduces U-MoLT, a U-shaped variant that separates memory construction from prediction and skips unused decoder traversals. Experiments include 400B-token pretraining compared with OLMo3 and continued pretraining of Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base, reporting better token efficiency and benchmark results. Code is publicly available. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose MoLT, using KV as cross-loop memory, reporting gains over OLMo3 in 400B-token pretraining and Qwen3.5 continued pretraining; code is released.

entry.title: Bound entanglement with negative partial transpose exists
entry.summary: Bound Entanglement with Negative Partial Transpose Exists arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper examines a Werner state on C^8 ⊗ C^8 with density matrix (23I − 3SWAP)/1448. It shows that this state has a negative partial transpose and is bound entangled, so no LOCC protocol can distill entanglement from any number of copies. Even with separable operations, the fidelity of a two-qubit output with a Bell state stays at or below about 0.604. The authors conclude that distillable entanglement is neither additive nor convex. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors exhibit a specific Werner state with negative partial transpose that is bound entangled, implying distillable entanglement is neither additive nor convex.

entry.title: Cairn: Frozen Robot Models Steered by Learned 3D Object Paths
entry.summary: Cairn: Object-Centric 3D Trajectory Priors for Steering Frozen VLAs arXiv · Nov 26, 2026Vision-language-action models often fail when objects are moved or obstacles appear, because they rely on training layouts. This paper introduces Cairn, which keeps the model frozen and guides it at test time along learned 3D trajectories of the held object, generated from scene point clouds, the object's grasp pose, and the instruction. Across 1,941 held-out LIBERO scenes, the success rate of a frozen π0.5 rises from 24.5% to 95.1%. It also transfers to a real Franka robot, where it avoids an obstacle and reaches a placement at the limit of the arm's reach. ★★★★ Notable: The authors steer a frozen VLA at test time with a learned object-centric 3D trajectory prior, reporting large success gains on 1,941 LIBERO scenes and a real Franka arm.

entry.title: Proof that computing normal-form correlated equilibria in extensive-form games is in PPAD
entry.summary: Computing Normal-Form Correlated Equilibria in Extensive-Form Games is in PPAD arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies how hard it is to find normal-form correlated equilibria (NFCE) in extensive-form games with perfect recall, a major open problem in algorithmic game theory. The authors show the problem lies in the PPAD class for any number of players. They also prove that computing such an NFCE whose support size is quadratic in the game size is PPAD-hard, even for two-player games. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show that computing normal-form correlated equilibria in extensive-form games lies in PPAD, and prove PPAD-hardness for two-player games with quadratic support.

entry.title: Estimating object material from drop videos, trained in simulation
entry.summary: What a Drop Reveals: Sim-to-Real Material Estimation for Deformable Objects from Video arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper estimates a deformable object's density-normalized stiffness E/ρ and, when impact causes plastic deformation, its yield stress σY/ρ from one real video of the object dropping. The predictor is trained only on simulated data. The authors find that synthetic validation ranks geometric inputs wrongly: 3D-lifted tracklets are most accurate in simulation but least accurate on real drops, while short 2D optical-flow tracklets transfer best. Their predictor, PhysReader, is closer to reference materials than other inputs and baselines on the real-object benchmark PhysReader-Real. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show simulation validation misranks geometric inputs, and propose PhysReader, trained in simulation, evaluated on their PhysReader-Real dataset against reference materials.

entry.title: Provably Efficient Offline Reinforcement Learning Under Recursive Entropic Risk
entry.summary: Provably Efficient Offline Discounted Reinforcement Learning under Recursive Entropic Risk arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies risk-sensitive reinforcement learning in discounted infinite-horizon Markov decision processes, using recursive entropic risk measures with parameter β≠0. It covers both risk-averse (β>0) and risk-seeking (β<0) settings in the offline setting, where a fixed dataset is used to learn a near-optimal policy. The authors propose a model-based algorithm, ERM-VI-LCB, and derive a PAC-type sample complexity bound, along with a matching lower bound showing exponential dependence on |β|/(1-γ) is unavoidable in the worst case. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give sample complexity upper and lower bounds for offline RL under recursive entropic risk, covering both risk-averse and risk-seeking settings.

entry.title: Recovering the full structure of linearized Reed-Solomon codes
entry.summary: Full Structure Recovery of Linearized Reed-Solomon Codes arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies the structure of linearized Reed-Solomon (LRS) codes, which are optimal sum-rank-metric codes generalizing Reed-Solomon and Gabidulin codes. The authors propose a polynomial-time procedure that recovers the full structure of an LRS code from only an arbitrary generator matrix. The results show that, like Hamming and rank-metric codes, LRS codes cannot be used directly in McEliece-like encryption. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors give a polynomial-time full structure recovery of LRS codes from any generator matrix, combining Overbeck-type attacks with shortening, ruling out direct McEliece-style use.

entry.title: Linguistic Knowledge Benchmark: Testing whether language models know early-grade literacy basics
entry.summary: The Linguistic Knowledge Benchmark: Do Language Models Know the Foundations of Early-Grade Literacy? arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper introduces the Linguistic Knowledge Benchmark, a largely automated pipeline that builds a vetted question set from curriculum documents, teacher guides and pupil books, organised by nine linguistic domains and seven grade levels. It was applied to Kiswahili (135 items) and English (137 items), evaluating 121 and 119 models. Frontier models exceed 90% accuracy in both languages, but smaller and cheaper models perform much worse, especially in Kiswahili. The authors release a sample of items, pipeline prompts, code, and a public leaderboard. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build a literacy-grounded linguistic benchmark and report 121 and 119 models on Kiswahili and English, with small models markedly weaker in Kiswahili.

entry.title: Proof that AC⁰ is not contained in BQAC⁰/qpoly via sublinear-degree Pauli approximation
entry.summary: mathsfAC⁰ notsubseteq mathsfBQAC⁰/mathsfqpoly via Sublinear-Degree Pauli Approximation arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper proves that AC⁰ is not contained in BQAC⁰/qpoly in the single-copy, single-output model, using an explicit P-uniform family of linear-size monotone depth-2 CNFs. It approximates the acceptance operator of any QAC⁰ circuit by an advice-independent Hermitian operator of sublinear Pauli degree. The same approximation gives two stretched-exponential bounds for QAC⁰ circuits acting on m-qubit states. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a sublinear-Pauli-degree operator approximation for QAC⁰ circuits with quantum advice, separating AC⁰ from BQAC⁰/qpoly and deriving two stretched-exponential bounds.

entry.title: Guidance as Variance Matching: A Rule for Choosing Diffusion Guidance Scales
entry.summary: Guidance as Variance Matching arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies how guidance improves diffusion models, which steers predictions away from a weaker reference prediction to raise sample quality. The authors find that at practical scales guidance worsens the posterior-mean prediction while samples improve. They introduce variance-matched guidance, a closed-form rule that chooses the guidance scale by matching the variance of guided predictions to that of the data, and it reproduces the hand-picked scales of eleven widely used models. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a closed-form variance-matching rule that recovers hand-picked guidance scales of eleven models without tuning, and offer a new mechanism interpretation.

entry.title: CIRKDV2: Cross-image relational knowledge distillation with context modeling for efficient segmentation
entry.summary: CIRKDV2: Cross-Image Relational Knowledge Distillation with Contextual Modeling for Efficient Semantic Segmentation arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proposes CIRKDV2, a knowledge distillation method for semantic segmentation that lets a small student network mimic a large teacher's structured semantic relations. Unlike methods that use only one image at a time, it transfers pixel-to-pixel, pixel-to-region, and channel-to-channel relations modeled across global images in the dataset. It also uses context aggregation to enrich student pixel features, reducing the semantic gap with the teacher. Experiments on Cityscapes, ADE20K, Pascal VOC, and COCO-Stuff-164K show it outperforms prior segmentation distillation methods across various architectures. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend relational distillation across images with contextual feature distillation, reporting gains over prior methods on four segmentation datasets.

entry.title: RevFlow: Generating Images by Reversing a Frozen Encoder's Layers
entry.summary: Generation as Reverse Encoding arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper introduces RevFlow, which treats generation as reverse encoding by using the intermediate representations of a frozen encoder as successive generative targets. It first generates deep semantic representations, then shallow ones that keep appearance and spatial detail, before decoding to pixels. A unified HyC-DiT model with a shared DiT backbone and stage-specific condition injection learns these transitions. On ImageNet 256×256, the authors report FID scores of 1.96 (690M) and 1.74 (1.55B) after 5 training epochs.. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose staged reverse generation through frozen encoder intermediate representations, with a shared DiT backbone, reporting ImageNet 256 FID results.

entry.title: TASK Memory: Text Memory Plus Activation Steering and Knowledge Editing to Reduce Memory Hallucination
entry.summary: TASK Memory: Beyond Text-Only Memory with Activation Steering and Knowledge Editing against Memory Hallucination arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies how LLM agents hallucinate about external memory even when the correct memory is retrieved, identifying memory-ignoring, memory-misapplying, and version-confusion failures. It proposes TASK memory, which pairs a text note with activation steering and knowledge editing that share one in-model address, using steering vectors to decide per query whether the model adopts the memory. On frozen models, the authors report large reductions in memory-ignoring and neighbour-misuse hallucinations, along with gains over BM25 RAG and multi-hop accuracy on MQuAKE. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine text memory with activation steering and removable knowledge editing sharing one in-model address, reporting reduced memory hallucination across five open models and multiple datas

entry.title: From NP-hard to exactly solvable via sample abundance: a theory paper on noisy parity fitting
entry.summary: From NP-Hardness to Exact Tractability Through Sample Abundance arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper studies noisy parity fitting, a worst-case NP-hard optimization problem. It shows that additional independent observations can make exact optimization tractable without changing the objective or feasible set. The authors give the number of extra readings needed for exact optimization with high probability, along with the computational cost. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show noisy parity fitting becomes exactly solvable with enough random samples, giving a tight sample-complexity order under a uniform rank-one sign tensor model.

entry.title: Spec2Weights: Proving That Networks a Language Model Writes from a Specification Are Exact
entry.summary: Spec2Weights: Certifying Networks that a Language Model Writes from a Specification arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper studies whether a language model can write the weights of small neural networks directly from a plain-language specification, without data or gradient training. It introduces methods to prove such networks exact under float32 arithmetic, using enumeration, dynamic programming, SMT proofs and induction. The authors certify 12 of 15 written networks on stated input domains. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report certifying float32 exactness over stated input domains for 12 of 15 LM-written networks and 25 of 30 new specifications, a novel verification angle.

entry.title: ShowNow: Fast-Responding Interactive Video Generation via Speculative Streaming
entry.summary: ShowNow: Fine-Grained Speculative Streaming for Responsive World Models arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper introduces ShowNow, a framework for interactive world models that generates video continuously while responding to user actions. It uses computation during playback to prepare action-conditioned future frames before input arrives, with single-latent commitment enabling frequent decisions. In ViZDoom, the full deployment reduces median input-to-display latency from 620 ms to 208 ms compared with the SolarWM-FT baseline. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prepare multiple action-conditioned futures during playback to cut input latency in interactive world models, reporting ViZDoom median latency falling from 620 to 208 ms.

entry.title: RoboEvo²: Robots improving themselves by co-evolving their policies and control harnesses
entry.summary: RoboEvo²: Recursive Robot Self-Improvement via Harness-Policy Co-Evolution arXiv · Nov 26, 2026The paper proposes RoboEvo², a framework in which a robot's control policy and its harness (coding agent and control APIs) evolve together recursively, without extra human demonstrations. Policy failures guide the coding agent to search for alternative solutions, which are consolidated into reusable skills, while verified trajectories train the policy. On LIBERO-PRO, standalone success rises from 11.0% to 84.1% and hybrid success from 30.4% to 90.5%. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose recursive harness-policy co-evolution with counterfactual preference distillation, reporting large success gains on LIBERO-PRO and RoboTwin.

entry.title: Paper showing the asymptotic spectrum of tensors is path-connected
entry.summary: The asymptotic spectrum of tensors is connected arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper proves that the asymptotic spectrum of complex tensors of every fixed order k≥3 is path-connected, so every spectral point links by a path to each one-leg-versus-rest flattening rank. As a result, the asymptotic spectrum at any fixed tensor is a closed interval, answering a question of Strassen. The authors also develop a general interpolation method between spectral points and use it to give new results and simpler proofs about rectangular matrix multiplication and polynomial multiplication. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove path-connectedness of the asymptotic tensor spectrum for every fixed order, answering Strassen, via a general interpolation method.

entry.title: VisualMontage: Using Authentic Image Sequences to Manipulate Vision-Language Agents' Beliefs
entry.summary: VisualMontage: Manipulating the Beliefs of Vision-Language Agents with Authentic Image Sequences arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper studies how vision-language model agents that interpret social-media posts can be misled by coordinated posts combining real images with accurate-looking captions. The authors build a benchmark of 544 target cases and 33.2K candidate images across eight domains. They also propose VisualMontage, a multi-agent framework that simulates such attacks. Experiments across 12 models show the attacks transfer between models, with mean success rates of 61.93% for proprietary and 68.71% for open-weight models. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce visual cognitive collusion, using authentic image sequences to steer vision-language agents; reported experiments span 544 cases and 12 models.

entry.title: DéjàVu: Reaching Majority Agreement by Repeating an Opinion
entry.summary: DéjàVu: Plurality Consensus by First Repetition arXiv · Nov 26, 2026This paper analyzes DéjàVu, a simple protocol in which each agent samples one random agent per round and adopts the first opinion it sees twice, then resets its memory. The rule needs no frequency counters or knowledge of population size or number of opinions. The authors prove that, when the initial plurality has a sufficient lead, the protocol reaches consensus on that opinion quickly with high probability, and is asymptotically never slower than h-majority protocols under the same conditions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a counter-free plurality consensus protocol using first repetition, proving convergence bounds and comparing them to h-majority dynamics.

entry.title: Long-range robot planning using graph anchors in latent world models
entry.summary: Long-Horizon Planning with Latent World Models via Graph Anchors arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper argues that latent world model planners judge progress by latent distance to the goal, which loses directional signal far from the goal and overweights the robot arm over the manipulated object during contact. The authors propose Graph Anchors, a training-free planner that builds a sparse graph over training frames and aims each step at a node a few moves ahead on the shortest path to the goal. On goals up to 400 steps away, success rose from 13% to 85% on PointMaze-Medium, from 8% to 87% on PointMaze-Large, and from 5% to 71% on Push-T. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a training-free planner aiming at nearby graph nodes instead of distant goals, and report large success gains on PointMaze and Push-T.

entry.title: Known-design attacks on LLM watermarks, and a sentence-keyed defense
entry.summary: Know the Design, Pick the Attack: Sentence-Keyed Watermarks for LLMs arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies watermarks that let a language model's provider recognise text the model wrote. It considers an attacker who reads the published watermark design and chooses between erasing hard-to-learn watermarks and forging ones that survive rewording. The authors propose KeyedLex, which takes its secret key from the grammar of the previous sentence, a feature rewording changes little, and whose detector need not recover the key exactly. They report that it outperforms the compared watermarks on both models tested. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use the previous sentence's grammar as a key against combined rewording and forgery attacks; the abstract reports outperforming compared watermarks on two models.

entry.title: Efficient Data Fusion in Distributionally Robust Optimization
entry.summary: Efficient Data Fusion in Distributionally Robust Optimization arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how to combine fragmented evidence, such as samples from different populations or privacy-protected summary statistics, for decision-making under uncertainty. It uses distributionally robust optimization, building one ambiguity set per source and hedging against all distributions in their intersection. The authors derive affine-rule upper bounds that decompose across ambiguity sets and are exact for quadratic losses over Wasserstein balls around Gaussian references. Experiments in portfolio, newsvendor, and classification settings show the approximation stays close to the exact value where computable, scales better, and outperforms aggregation-based benchmarks out-of-sample. ★★★★ Notable: The authors reformulate multi-source distributionally robust optimization via functional Lagrange multipliers, give decomposable affine upper bounds, and report near-exact values and out-of-sample gai

entry.title: Who Wears the Camera? Locating Camera Wearers Across Views Beyond Humans
entry.summary: Who Is Ego? Scaling Cross-View Camera Wearer Identification and Segmentation beyond Humans arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper addresses identifying who or what wears a first-person camera, using a synchronized third-person image, for wearers including robots, vehicles, animals and drones. It introduces FindEgo-1M, a dataset of 1.16M real and simulated ego-exo image pairs. The proposed EgoRay-ZS method is training-free, and the full EgoRay model reports higher accuracy and speed than the compared baselines. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use the epipole geometry to identify camera wearers across views, reusing a frozen 3D reconstruction model training-free, and report gains on a new large dataset.

entry.title: Computing fair allocations of goods under budget-style size limits
entry.summary: Computing Feasible EF1 Allocations under Generalized Assignment Constraints arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies fairly dividing indivisible goods when each agent's bundle must fit within her budget and goods can have different sizes for different agents, with unallocated goods going to charity. It shows that feasible envy-freeness up to one good (FEF1) allocations can be computed in strongly polynomial time, provided each agent's value can be almost exactly maximized over her feasible bundles. The allocation can also be made approximately envy-free up to any good while keeping nearly half the Nash welfare of a given allocation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend FEF1 computability to agent-specific sizes, giving a strongly polynomial algorithm, a near-tight quadratic repair bound, and NP-hardness results.

entry.title: Noise threshold for quantum-memory-assisted learning
entry.summary: Noise threshold for learning with quantum memory arXiv · Nov 25, 2026Quantum memories can exponentially reduce the number of experiments needed to learn a physical process, but real memories are noisy. The paper shows that for Pauli memory noise, this advantage depends on the sum of the squared eigenvalues. It proves that when this sum is at most one, no protocol with an entangled probe gains an exponential advantage. Experiments on a superconducting processor and a three-qubit repetition code are also reported. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive a noise threshold for quantum-memory learning advantage under Pauli noise, prove no exponential gain below it, and report superconducting-processor experiments.

entry.title: Exact exponents for trace-distance errors in quantum information tasks
entry.summary: Exponential Analysis for Trace-Distance Errors in Quantum Information Theory arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies trace-distance errors in classical-quantum soft covering, privacy amplification against quantum side information, convex splitting, and decoupling by Haar-random unitaries followed by partial trace. For independent and identically distributed settings, it determines exact reliability functions and strong converse exponents for these tasks. The reliability formulas involve sandwiched Rényi information, while the strong converse exponents involve Petz-Rényi information. The proofs link trace-distance errors to quantum hypothesis testing. ★★★★ Notable: The authors determine exact reliability functions and strong converse exponents for several quantum tasks, using sandwiched and Petz-Rényi information and hypothesis testing.

entry.title: Convergence of second-order training methods for physics-informed neural networks as network width grows
entry.summary: Global Convergence of Second-Order Methods for Physics-Informed Neural Networks in the Overparameterized Limit arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper analyzes the convergence of regularized Newton and Gauss-Newton methods for training physics-informed neural networks that solve partial differential equations. As the number of hidden units goes to infinity, training converges in probability to a deterministic limit equation involving a Newton neural tangent kernel operator. The authors prove that the PDE residual vanishes during training and that the network converges to the PDE solution under mild assumptions. They also show that a sufficiently small regularization parameter makes the residual's projections onto leading eigenfunctions decay exponentially, so the parameter acts as a spectral filter. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a convergence analysis for regularized Newton and Gauss-Newton training of PINNs in the overparameterized limit, with explicit rates and a spectral-filter interpretation.

entry.title: Optimal (1,1)-criss-cross deletion-correcting codes with linear-time encoding and decoding
entry.summary: Optimal texorpdfstring(1,1)(1,1)-Criss-Cross Deletion-Correcting Codes with Linear-Time Encoder and Decoder arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper studies q-ary n×n arrays subject to a (1,1)-criss-cross deletion, which removes one row and one column. It first derives a sphere-packing type lower bound on the redundancy of codes correcting such deletions. It then gives two constructions: the first has redundancy 2n-1+2log_q n+o_q(1), matching the bound up to a vanishing term, with O_q(n^2) decoding; the second has redundancy 2n+2log_q n+O_q(1), with O_q(n^2) encoding and decoding. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a sphere-packing lower bound on redundancy for (1,1)-criss-cross deletion codes and construct near-tight codes with linear-time encoding and decoding.

entry.title: Decision-focused learning for multistage stochastic planning, applied to power grid repair scheduling
entry.summary: Decision-Focused Learning for Multistage Stochastic Programs, with Application to Power Network Repair Scheduling arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper proposes a decision-focused learning framework for multistage stochastic programs with discrete decisions, where a neural network predicts scores for the part of the decision that drives state transitions. The network is trained on labels from offline single-scenario problems using the Fenchel-Young loss with perturbed optimizers. Applied to repairing failed components in a 5-bus and an IEEE 14-bus power network, with and without a per-stage repair budget, the method is the cheapest policy under a binding budget, 14% to 23% below the next-best policy. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend decision-focused learning to multistage stochastic programs, training a network with Fenchel-Young loss and applying it to power network repair scheduling under budget constraints.

entry.title: Proof of the functional batch conjecture and its extension to all finite fields
entry.summary: The Functional Batch Conjecture And Its Extension To All Finite Fields arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper studies a coding scheme in which servers store all nonzero linear combinations of s information symbols over a finite field. The authors prove that this code is a functional batch code for every finite field and every s≥1, with list size (q^s+q-2)/2, and that this list size cannot be increased. They also determine the minimum length of such functional batch codes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend the functional batch conjecture to all finite fields, reporting tight list sizes and minimum code lengths with proofs.

entry.title: AgentLens: Graph-guided security auditing framework for LLM-based agents
entry.summary: AgentLens: Graph-guided Security Auditing for LLM-based Agents arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents AgentLens, a framework for systematically auditing security in LLM-based agents before deployment. It builds an Audit Knowledge Graph from the agent's implementation, component interactions, and built-in defenses, then derives attack paths and generates validation payloads tested in multi-turn scenarios. Across five popular agent applications, AgentLens found 44 vulnerabilities, all triggered during execution, detecting 3.67 times more than the prior approach AgentFuzz. Twelve of the reported issues have been assigned CVE IDs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose an audit knowledge graph guiding attack-path validation, reporting 44 vulnerabilities across five popular agents, 3.67 times AgentFuzz.

entry.title: Single-database rewards can be gamed; counterfactual execution aims to make text-to-SQL RL trustworthy
entry.summary: Single-Database Rewards Are Hackable: Counterfactual Execution for Trustworthy Text-to-SQL RL arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper argues that reinforcement learning rewards for text-to-SQL agents, which check query results on a single database, can be satisfied by wrong queries that match by luck when the data lack revealing rows. The authors propose a counterfactual-database reward that also runs the final query on several hidden, code-generated database copies, paying only if all results match (strict form) or by the share matched (mean form). On 1,302 synthetic audit questions, the strict form substantially reduces buggy queries receiving full reward and reward hacks, without rejecting any of 2,847 correct queries. ★★★★ Notable: The authors add hidden counterfactual database copies to verify SQL rewards and curb reward hacking. They report results on 1,302 synthetic audit questions and three-seed GRPO comparisons.

entry.title: Navigent: A geometry-grounded agent framework for vision-language navigation
entry.summary: Navigent: A Geometry-Grounded Agentic Framework for Vision Language Navigation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents Navigent, an agentic framework for vision-and-language navigation built on a frozen multimodal large language model. Its Geometry-Grounded Execution Critic checks whether measured movement matches commanded actions and whether tracked visual landmarks align with world coordinates, triggering reobservation, local adjustment, or recovery when discrepancies appear. An offline procedure refines prompts and critic logic from successful and failed trajectories without changing model weights. Navigent reports 84.0% and 86.0% success rates on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE validation-unseen splits. ★★★★ Notable: The authors add geometry-based consistency checks to a frozen MLLM navigator, reporting high SR and SPL on R2R-CE and RxR-CE unseen validation splits.

entry.title: Whether models predict drug targets or already know the answer
entry.summary: Did the Model Forecast It, or Already Know It? Evaluating Large Language Models for Novel Drug-Target Prioritisation with a Temporal Knowledge-Graph Oracle arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper tests whether language models can forecast the first clinical trial of a drug target for a disease, using a dated biomedical knowledge graph rebuilt at the end of each year from 2020. Six open models were evaluated with and without the graph, predicting trials in the following year. Without retrieval, the models performed about as well as a simple past-trial count baseline, and pre-decision evidence added little. The newest graph lifted most models above that baseline, but its paths often contained the post-decision trial itself. The authors recommend dating both features and labels in target prioritisation evaluations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors recast target-disease hypotheses as dated first-trial events, test temporal forecasting, and report that graph paths often leak the outcome.

entry.title: SOLO: Sample-faithful, detectable LLM watermarking for repeated sampling
entry.summary: SOLO: Towards Sample-Faithful and Detectable LLM Watermarking under Repeated Sampling via Content-Anchored Single-Owner Contexts arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper shows that standard distortion-free watermarks for language models make multiple responses to the same prompt interfere with each other, because shared answer templates cause their watermark contexts to collide. The authors propose SOLO, which keeps a request-level context history but anchors keyed contexts on content chosen by min-hash, so sibling responses rarely compete and random edits stay local. Experiments on five language models from three families and three benchmarks report that SOLO preserves self-consistency and uncertainty estimation and, at a 1% false positive rate, detects more responses than four-token key pools on most tasks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose content-anchored single-owner contexts for repeated sampling watermarks, evaluated on five models and three benchmarks against key pools and context history.

entry.title: Detectable by Design: Learning a Continuous 3D Saliency Field
entry.summary: Detectable by Design: Learning a Continuous 3D Saliency Field from 2D Detector Responses arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper defines 3D saliency as image detectability, meaning how strongly a 2D interest-point detector responds to a surface point across all views where it is visible. The authors propose DetField, a continuous field that takes a point cloud as input and predicts detectability at any 3D location, using multi-scale curvature invariants in its decoder. In a localization benchmark isolating 3D point selection, DetField outperforms Harris-3D and five learned keypoint methods on objects and real indoor scenes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors define 3D saliency as 2D detector response and learn a continuous field, reporting gains over Harris-3D and learned keypoint methods on localization benchmarks.

entry.title: Improving speculative drafting with hidden state mixing and gradient detach
entry.summary: Improving Tail-Augmented Speculative Drafting with Hidden State Mixing and Gradient Detach arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper addresses a training-inference mismatch in multi-token prediction and EAGLE-style drafters used for speculative decoding. It proposes two training-only methods, Hidden State Mixing (HSM) and Hidden State Gradient Detach (HSGD), which add no inference cost. HSGD gives the highest acceptance rates at early draft positions, while HSM performs best later in the draft. Across several Nemotron models and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, HSM improves mean acceptance length by up to 52.2% over co-trained MTP. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose training-only hidden state mixing and gradient detach to reduce drafter train-inference mismatch, reporting acceptance length gains across several models versus EAGLE-3's TTT.

entry.title: Accelerated multiobjective sampling over probability measures via Hilbert-space lifting
entry.summary: Accelerated Proximal Gradient Methods for Multiobjective Optimization over Probability Measures via Hilbert-Space Lifting arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper treats finding one distribution that balances several targets as Pareto multiobjective optimization of KL divergences over probability measures. It proposes multiobjective Wasserstein proximal gradient (MWPG) and its accelerated version MWAPG, which lift measures to pushforwards of a base measure by maps in a Hilbert space, yielding a constrained composite problem over transport maps. The authors prove discrete-time convergence rates, including O(1/k^2) for convex smooth potentials and linear rates under strong convexity. Experiments report that MWAPG needs far fewer iterations than MWPG and matches or beats A-MWGraD in Bayesian multi-task learning. ★★★★ Notable: The authors lift measures to Hilbert-space maps, yielding accelerated proximal methods with O(1/k^2) and linear discrete-time rates, tested on Bayesian multi-task learning.

entry.title: End-to-end image-goal navigation for agile quadrotors using recurrent state distillation
entry.summary: End-to-End Image-Goal Navigation for Agile Quadrotors via Recurrent State Distillation arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents a policy that navigates a quadrotor in unseen 3D environments toward a goal photograph by directly commanding thrust and angular rates, without state estimation or a separate velocity controller. The recurrent vision-based policy is trained through a four-stage pipeline combining geometric and motion supervision, privileged-teacher distillation, and end-to-end reinforcement learning fine-tuning. It achieves an 82.3% success rate over 1000 held-out flights, with a mean terminal position error of 0.10 m for successful flights. Deployed zero-shot on a real quadrotor, it reaches an 84% success rate over 25 trials in an unseen indoor environment. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present the first image-goal policy commanding thrust and rates on quadrotors in unseen 3D settings, reporting 82.3% success over 1000 flights and 84% real-robot trials.

entry.title: JHealthBench-L: Clinician-Reviewed Japanese Localization of HealthBench for Medical LLM Evaluation
entry.summary: JHealthBench-L: Clinician-Reviewed Localization of HealthBench for Rubric-Based Medical LLM Evaluation in Japan arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper presents JHealthBench-L, a Japan-localized version of the HealthBench benchmark for evaluating large language models on open-ended health consultations. It contains 79 patient-facing consultations and 1,022 physician-style criteria, drafted with LLMs and then selected, revised, and independently reviewed by physicians. The authors compare it with a machine-translated baseline across 18 LLMs and report that translation alone keeps coarse model rankings but changes verdicts on 17.7% of modified criteria. ★★★★ Notable: The authors localize HealthBench rubrics for Japan with physician review and show machine translation masks item-level errors, reporting results across 18 LLMs.

entry.title: PatternMiner: An AI System That Combines LLM Agents and Small Models to Discover Math Theorems
entry.summary: PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces PatternMiner, a system in which an LLM agent generates mathematical datasets, trains small machine learning models on them, and uses interpretability techniques to extract patterns and formulate conjectures. The agent then searches for counterexamples with mathematical software and refines conjectures iteratively, attempting proofs along the way. Applied to five positivity problems in algebraic combinatorics, the system proves several new theorems, including results on Schubert positivity and projection, a character-row evaluation formula, a restricted Kazhdan–Lusztig combinatorial invariance conjecture, and Schur positivity for a family of immanant coefficients. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine LLM agents with interpretable small models for open-ended conjecture discovery, reporting new theorems on positivity problems in algebraic combinatorics.

entry.title: BReD: Block Replay Dithering to Stabilize Low-Bit EMA Optimizer States
entry.summary: BReD: Block Replay Dithering for Stable Low-Bit EMA Optimizer States arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper shows that storing optimizer states in low-bit form is unstable because they are repeatedly dequantized, updated, and requantized each training step. For states updated by exponential moving averages, quantization errors accumulate recursively, especially when the decay factor is close to 1. The authors propose BReD, which adapts subtractive dithering using deterministic seed replay and block-wise shared dither values to reduce rounding bias and control variance. Experiments report that 4-bit BReD closely matches full-precision optimizer training across the evaluated pretraining and fine-tuning settings, and 3-bit BReD also converges stably in those settings. ★★★★ Notable: The authors adapt subtractive dithering to optimizer-state quantization using seed replay and block-shared dither, reporting PPL and downstream results across 120M to 7B models.

entry.title: Beyond the Happy Path: Teaching Robot World Models to Predict Manipulation Failures
entry.summary: Beyond the Happy Path: Generalizing Robot World Models from Simulated Failures arXiv · Nov 25, 2026The paper addresses how robot world models fail to predict outcomes when grasps go wrong, such as objects being pushed, tilted, or slipping. The authors build Reforge, a dataset of 62k simulated trajectories with perturbed grasps and ground-truth object pose and contact information. They propose WorldReforge, which adds two training signals, Interaction Alignment and Surface Correspondence, without extra inference cost. The method reduces object trajectory error by 28.2% overall, and it also improves reconstruction on DROID and real failure videos. ★★★★ Notable: The authors train robot world models on simulated failure trajectories with ground truth, adding interaction alignment and surface correspondence signals. They report 28.2% lower object trajectory err

entry.title: On the Learnability of Model Reprogramming: Reachability and Relabeling View
entry.summary: On the Learnability of Model Reprogramming: A Reachability and Relabeling Perspective arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how many target samples model reprogramming needs, where a frozen source model is adapted via a learnable input transformation and output mapping. It factorizes the wrapper hypothesis class complexity into a reachability term over source-label patterns and a conditional relabeling term, yielding an agnostic PAC estimation bound matched by a lower bound. It also decomposes the approximation error into source-label information loss and output-mapping restriction, with an upper bound. ★★★★ Notable: The authors decompose wrapper sample complexity into reachability and relabeling terms, reporting an agnostic PAC bound matched by a lower bound and an exact approximation-error decomposition.

entry.title: Testing whether driving models truly understand roads they have not seen
entry.summary: Off the Driven Path: Transferable Road Understanding in Driving VLAs arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper introduces Road-KSU, a framework that turns HD maps and actor annotations into road-centric scene graphs for question answering and trajectory compliance evaluation. On NAVSIM, nearly all test samples lie close to training samples, and planner scores on turns rise with the number of training drives through the same location, suggesting memorized road geometry. Experiments on geographically disjoint splits show action performance drops most on unfamiliar turns, and the authors conclude that geographic diversity is key to transferable road knowledge. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce Road-KSU and geographically disjoint splits, reporting on NAVSIM that planners rely on memorized road geometry and that place diversity drives transferable road knowledge.

entry.title: Spoofing Wireless Sensing via Metasurface-Based Physical Deepfakes
entry.summary: Spoofing Wireless Sensing with Metasurface-based Physical Deepfakes arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies security risks in wireless sensing, where existing communication signals are used to capture information about a device's surroundings. The authors show that attackers can use programmable metasurfaces to control the amplitude and phase of victim wireless channels, reproducing pre-recorded genuine events at the physical layer. Unlike earlier attacks that target single channel features, this approach works regardless of the features the victim system uses. The attack is validated in a lab study on MIMO channels and with off-the-shelf Wi-Fi sensing, challenging the trustworthiness of wireless sensing. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose metasurface-based physical deepfake attacks reproducing real events at the physical layer, independent of features; validated on MIMO lab and Wi-Fi sensing.

entry.title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
entry.summary: Same behavior, different mechanism: what finite experiments can certify about how a network computes arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper examines whether mechanism-level quantities used in interpretability and machine consciousness assessment, specifically the integrated information φ from integrated information theory, can be identified and certified from finite, partial and noisy experiments. Using stochastic networks of four and five units with known ground truth, the authors show that identical input-output behavior can hide different mechanisms and that partial recordings can impose precision floors. They also prove that φ can be certified as a lower bound over a region of mechanisms from finite controlled transition data. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose identifiability, continuity, and certifiability criteria, and report exact characterizations and finite-data lower-bound certificates for integrated information in small networks.

entry.title: Kairos: a planner orchestrator that picks among engines to handle all kinds of PDDL tasks
entry.summary: Kairos: Fast and Reliable Symbolic Task Planning for Autonomous Robots arXiv · Oct 29, 2026The paper presents Kairos, a system that profiles each PDDL planning task and selects among five planning engines to cover everything from STRIPS to PDDL+. Every candidate plan is checked by a validator independent of the planner's transformations.
