The authors report state-of-the-art results on xBD and BRIGHT under both optical-optical and optical-SAR settings. ★★★★ Notable: The authors align text damage descriptions with building regions via instance-adaptive prototypes, reporting state-of-the-art results on xBD and BRIGHT for damage assessment.

entry.title: EviCraft: Can Minecraft Agents Find What They Cannot See?
entry.summary: EviCraft: Can Minecraft Agents Find What They Cannot See? arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper examines Minecraft, a common testbed for embodied agents, where tools such as mineBlock select targets from the simulator's loaded world state without a visibility check. As a result, agents can reach buried ores they have never seen, and scores cannot show whether they actually searched. The authors formalize a requirement called evidence closure and present EviCraft, a runtime and benchmark that compares a perception-grounded admission regime with a loaded-state regime reproducing standard tool stacks. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formalize evidence closure and compare perception-grounded and loaded-state regimes on Minecraft Survival, revealing tool-level state leakage.

entry.title: Stochastic gradient descent with large learning rates and faster convergence
entry.summary: SGD with Large Learning Rates: General Analysis & Improved Rates arXiv · Nov 25, 2026This paper studies how Stochastic Gradient Descent behaves when the learning rate is large, rather than below the usual curvature-based stability threshold. For the cross-entropy loss with linear predictors and two-layer neural networks, the authors prove an accelerated O(T^{-2}) convergence rate. Their analysis gives a fine-grained description of the stochastic large-stepsize dynamics, which also yields tighter guarantees within the stable regime. The results indicate that large-stepsize acceleration persists under stochastic noise and extends beyond linear models. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report an accelerated O(T^-2) rate for large-stepsize SGD with cross-entropy on linear and two-layer networks, answering an open question and improving stable-regime bounds.

entry.title: Contrastive Proxy Forests: Learning Confounder Proxies from Multimodal Records
entry.summary: Contrastive Proxy Forests: Completeness-Preserving Proxy Learning from Multimodal Records arXiv · Nov 24, 2026Proximal causal inference needs two proxy variables that capture an unmeasured confounder, but rich high-dimensional records such as clinical notes and physiological waveforms are hard to use directly. This paper proposes Contrastive Proxy Forests (CPF), which contrasts treatment-side and outcome-side modalities on a separate unlabeled sample to learn what they share, filtering out modality-specific style, and then feeds the resulting proxies into a proximal causal forest. The authors report that where style is strong, CPF reduces the error of conditional effects by 10-22% relative to PCA-based proxies. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use ridge CCA contrast to learn proximal proxies from multimodal records, proving exclusion preservation and reporting gains on MIMIC-IV.

entry.title: Universal Adversarial Attacks on Video Object Segmentation Aligned with Its Two-Stage Inference
entry.summary: Attack-Inference Aligned Universal Adversarial Attacks on Video Object Segmentation arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper proposes AUV, an adversarial framework that targets the two-stage inference of video object segmentation models: target initialization and memory-based propagation. It optimizes a universal adversarial perturbation using decoupled training for each stage, disrupting the shared memory space so the attack works across masks, points, boxes, and language prompts. On DAVIS17-val, it reduces mask-based SAM3 to 8.4 J&F, compared with 55.4 for the previous state of the art under the same setup. ★★★★ Notable: The authors align a universal adversarial perturbation with VOS's two-stage paradigm and report SAM3 dropping to 8.4 J&F on DAVIS17-val.

entry.title: How Massive Activations Relate to Adversarial Robustness
entry.summary: Understanding the Importance of Massive Activations through Adversarial Robustness arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies massive activations, a common phenomenon in Large Language Models, and explains their role using spline theory. The authors show that massive activations push representations away from network nonlinearity boundaries, reducing the complexity of the input-output map near data points. Experiments across several architectures and datasets show that massive activations co-occur with adversarial robustness, and their rise during LLM pretraining closely tracks adversarial accuracy under token embedding perturbations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors link massive activations to adversarial robustness and region migration, reporting the effect beyond transformers across several architectures and datasets, plus LLM pretraining experiment

entry.title: ContinualDrive: A multi-axis benchmark for updating deployed driving planners
entry.summary: ContinualDrive: A Deployment-Anchored, Multi-Axis Benchmark for Continual Updates of Learned Driving Planners arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper introduces ContinualDrive, a benchmark for continually updating learned driving planners after deployment. It updates PlanTF and Diffusion Planner on nuPlan logs one scenario group at a time and evaluates checkpoints in open and closed loop. The authors report that evaluation choices can reverse verdicts, and that in closed loop no update regime measurably beat the deployed planner. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce deployment-anchored evaluation with four measurement axes and a three-valued release verdict, testing two driving planners on nuPlan logs across multiple update regimes.

entry.title: Rewriting the PHP interpreter in safe Rust with a proof of logical memory safety
entry.summary: A Star is Reborn: The PHP Interpreter Rewritten in Safe Rust arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper addresses the many memory-safety vulnerabilities found in PHP's C interpreter by reimplementing it in safe Rust. It introduces logical memory safety, which confines program operations to their permitted memory, and formalizes this property through an abstract PHP machine model. The authors rewrote the PHP 5.0.0 engine in Rust and formally proved that, for a core fragment of PHP, the translation establishes logical memory safety. The Rust version matches the C implementation on functionality tests and evaluated applications, with an average runtime overhead of about 15%. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors formalize logical memory safety via an abstract PHP machine, prove refinement for a core fragment, and report results on 173 vulnerabilities with about 15% overhead.

entry.title: "A Mesh to Remember": a mesh-based memory method that keeps video worlds' appearance consistent
entry.summary: A Mesh to Remember: Persistent Appearance for Interactive Video Worlds arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper proposes M2R (Mesh to Remember), a few-step causal video renderer that stores its generated features on the surfaces they depict and retrieves them by rasterizing the mesh when those surfaces return to view. Appearance moves with objects, persists across revisits, and is shared by all agents observing the world. Trained only on synthetic data, M2R transfers zero-shot to real indoor scans and coding-agent-authored worlds, rendering 720p video at 40 FPS in real time. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose storing renderer features on mesh surfaces to persist appearance across revisits and agents, reporting consistency gains on static, dynamic, and multi-agent benchmarks at real-time

entry.title: Sequence design for flat-top beams: controlling passband ripple and stopband leakage together
entry.summary: Sequences for Flat-Top Beams arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies sequences for flat-top beams, which are used in radar and communication systems. Using Fourier analysis, the authors examine the asymptotic behavior of passband ripple and stopband leakage. They show that finite-alphabet sequences, including binary and quaternary ones, cannot make both quantities vanish simultaneously as length grows. For infinite-alphabet sequences, generalized step-chirp (GSC) sequences satisfy both requirements under specified conditions on length-bandwidth product and step size. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend sequence design beyond full-band flatness to flat-top beams, contrasting finite and infinite alphabets and giving GSC convergence rates.

entry.title: TESS: Query-Guided Temporal Event-Structured Frame Selection for Long Videos
entry.summary: TESS: Query-Guided Temporal Event-Structured Frame Selection for Long-Video Understanding arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper proposes TESS, a training-free framework that selects video frames for long-video understanding guided by the query. Under a fixed frame budget, it chooses frames that jointly show the reference event and the asked-about event in the required temporal order. Across four long-video benchmarks and three multimodal backbones, TESS outperforms the strongest baseline by 4.0 to 5.5 percentage points. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose training-free, role-aware temporal event-structured frame selection, reporting gains of 4.0-5.5 points over the strongest baseline on four long-video benchmarks.

entry.title: Per-Instruction Token Freezing for Faster Multi-Edit Image Editing
entry.summary: Every Edit Its Own Budget: Per-Instruction Token Freezing for Training-Free Acceleration of Multi-Edit Image Editing arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper addresses speeding up instruction-based image editing when one instruction requests several edits. It proposes TIDE, a training-free method that gives each instruction part its own compute budget, locating each part's region through the editor's attention via unbalanced optimal transport. Tokens are frozen once their drift is small relative to their own part, and a sparse engine computes only the rest. Experiments on FLUX.2 Klein and Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 report higher speed and fewer dropped edits than global-threshold approaches. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give each instruction part its own compute budget and characterize the optimal per-part threshold policy, reporting 4.81-4.89x speedups and fewer dropped edits across six benchmarks on two

entry.title: Can AI Design a Better nnU-Net? A Method That Turns Failures into Design Rules
entry.summary: Can AI Design a Better nnU-Net? A Hypothesis-Driven Architecture Discovery Loop from Failures to Design Rules arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents a loop in which LLM agents analyze structured error patterns, form testable hypotheses, and run counterfactual controls under a frozen nnU-Net pipeline. Validated mechanisms are distilled into executable trigger-to-action rules. For 3D medical image segmentation, the approach yields two principles and the resulting LeanNeXt and LeanNeXt+ models, which outperform nnU-Net on the reported CT/MRI benchmarks at lower cost. ★★★★ Notable: The authors turn failure analysis into falsifiable hypotheses and trigger-routed design rules, reporting gains over nnU-Net on 15 CT/MRI settings and over ResEnc-M on 12 of 15.

entry.title: From ELBO to Maximum Likelihood: Convergence Analysis of Variational Autoencoders for Nonlinear Mixed-Effects Models
entry.summary: From the ELBO to Maximum Likelihood: Convergence of Variational Autoencoders for Nonlinear Mixed-Effects Modeling arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper analyzes the convergence of the VAE-NLME algorithm for nonlinear mixed-effects models. The authors prove that the ELBO-based version converges almost surely to the set of stationary points of the ELBO, without assuming the encoder is trained exactly. The final algorithm trains the encoder by gradient optimization and uses it as a proposal for importance-weighted sufficient statistics, and it converges almost surely to stationary points of the marginal log-likelihood with no assumption on encoder training. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove almost sure convergence of a VAE-NLME algorithm to stationary points of the ELBO and marginal log-likelihood, relevant to pharmacometrics.

entry.title: ASTERISM: Do Multimodal LLMs Actually Look at All the Images?
entry.summary: ASTERISM: Do Multimodal LLMs Actually Look at All the Images? arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper audits about 33k items from 19 public multi-image benchmarks and finds that 24.2% can be answered from a single image or the question alone, which it calls the single-image shortcut. Based on these items, the authors build ASTERISM, a multi-image benchmark of 18.7k items, plus training data and ASTERISM-Lite, a hand-verified hard subset on which the strongest proprietary model scores 68%. They also propose cross-image credit assignment (CICA), a reinforcement learning extension that shifts reward toward tokens requiring multiple images, raising the ASTERISM score by 2.6 to 6.0 points on three open-source models. ★★★★ Notable: The authors audit multi-image benchmarks for a single-image shortcut and propose cross-image credit assignment, reporting gains on three open-source MLLMs across 19 benchmarks.

entry.title: Who gets the information? An α-fair framework for selecting features that cover all labels in multi-label data
entry.summary: Who gets the information? An α-fair label-coverage framework for multi-label feature selection arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper examines how information-theoretic filters for multi-label feature selection distribute relevance across labels, and treats these choices as implicit social welfare functions. It proposes FLIC, which greedily maximises the α-fair welfare of per-label information coverage, with α moving the selection from utilitarian to max-min. Experiments on 22 data sets report that FLIC performs best among the compared information-theoretic filters on most metrics. ★★★★ Notable: The authors unify multi-label relevance terms as alpha-fair welfare, prove submodularity and a 1-1/e guarantee, and report comparisons across 22 data sets.

entry.title: When permission replies rewrite the agent's rules: how a single approval can disable coding-agent safeguards
entry.summary: When Answering Is Administering: Permission Replies That Rewrite Coding-Agent Policy arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper shows that coding agents let plugins and remote services answer permission prompts, and that checking each answer separately fails over a whole session. One answer can rewrite the policy used for all later answers, for example by deleting a deny rule that protects secrets. The authors prove two tight bounds on what safe delegation requires and confirm their predictions across thirteen permission designs in ten agent systems. Enforcing these bounds at the shared update step blocks the attack. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show per-decision checks fail across a run and prove two tight bounds on delegated policy updates. They report validating predictions across thirteen permission designs in ten agent system

entry.title: Authorizing LLM Agents Across Context Compaction
entry.summary: LLM Agent Authorization Across Context Compaction arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper shows that authorizers which derive permissions from the user's request, such as Progent, fail when an agent's context is automatically compacted, because the compactor's summary is treated as the user speaking. In experiments, the derived policy admitted an attacker's account in 91% of cases when a frontier compactor's summary was used. The authors prove a bound showing that an authorizer unable to tell forged records from legitimate ones cannot separate them beyond a limit. Their fix credits only authenticated user text carried verbatim across compaction, and in 40 attacked AgentDojo episodes no attacker action completed. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show compaction summaries are mistaken for user speech, prove a tight indistinguishability bound, and propose trusting only verbatim authenticated user text.

entry.title: Self-orthogonal minimal codes built from n-to-1 mappings
entry.summary: Self-Orthogonal Minimal Codes from n-to-1 Mappings arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies linear codes derived from n-to-1 mappings over finite fields that are both self-orthogonal and minimal. Such codes can simultaneously yield quantum error-correcting codes and secret-sharing schemes. The authors use right greatest common divisors of skew polynomials to determine the kernel dimensions of associated linearized polynomials, which gives the codes' weight distributions. They treat two newly constructed families and one known family, proving that all resulting codes are minimal and self-orthogonal. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use right gcds of skew polynomials to find kernel dimensions, deriving weight distributions and proving minimal, self-orthogonal codes for three n-to-1 families.

entry.title: Benchmarking protein structure tokenizers as targets for language-model generation
entry.summary: Benchmarking Protein Structure Tokenizers as Generation Targets for Language Models arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper compares eight discrete tokenizers that convert protein three-dimensional structure into tokens a language model can generate residue by residue. Holding the base model, data and training recipe fixed, the authors swap only the tokenizer and train a 9B model across several compute budgets and evaluation sets, measuring writability by TM score. The tokenizers differ substantially in writability, and the authors find that local structure preservation in the code space, rather than codebook size or reconstruction quality, best explains the differences. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose writability, not reconstruction, as the criterion for structure tokenizers, swapping only the tokenizer across 96 cells and reporting local code-space structure as the explanatory

entry.title: Fast Encrypted Fixed-Point Multiplication Without Quadratic Cost
entry.summary: Encrypted Fixed-Point Multiplication in Quasilinear Complexity arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper addresses the high computational overhead of homomorphic encryption for high-precision fixed-point arithmetic. The authors introduce focused encoding, which concentrates precision at one embedding, together with an error-shaping technique to preserve it. They present an encrypted fixed-point multiplication algorithm for the CKKS scheme and a bootstrapping method for focused encoding that aims to avoid the quadratic cost of conventional bootstrapping. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce focused encoding and error shaping, giving CKKS fixed-point multiplication in online time O(n log n) with bootstrapping.

entry.title: Letting Pixels Through: Rethinking Long Skip Connections in Pixel Diffusion Models
entry.summary: Let The Pixels Through: Rethinking Long Skip Connections for Scalable Pixel Diffusion arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper revisits long skip connections in U-Net and finds that their commonly assumed optimization benefit is not needed for denoising. It proposes asymmetric long skips and adaGLU, a SwiGLU-like block that filters embedding information before it is added to decoder features. The resulting pixel diffusion transformer scales to 1.6B parameters when trained from scratch and reaches 1.62 and 1.70 FID on ImageNet-256 and ImageNet-512, with support for text and image inputs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors redesign long skip connections with asymmetric skips and adaGLU, reporting 1.62 and 1.70 FID on ImageNet-256 and -512 at up to 1.6B parameters.

entry.title: Bit-flip attacks on quantized neural networks without model parameters
entry.summary: Bit-Flip Attacks on Quantized Neural Networks without Knowledge of Model Parameters arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper shows that quantization asymmetry makes small high-precision tensors especially vulnerable to bit flips. It introduces CoarseHammer, an attack that needs no parameter values, gradients, or data, and remains effective under continued fine-tuning. Across ten models, including four large language models, median successful runs need at most 24 flips to reach chance accuracy. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show quantization asymmetry concentrates bit-flip vulnerability in small high-precision tensors and propose a parameter-free attack, reporting results on ten models and real systems.

entry.title: When the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound holds for linear stabilizer codes, and how far it can fail
entry.summary: Validity and maximum violation of the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound for linear stabilizer codes arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper examines whether linear entanglement-assisted stabilizer codes satisfy the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound of Brun, Devetak and Hsieh, which estimates how many pre-shared entangled pairs a code needs. The answer depends on how many qudits, together with the receiver's halves of the pairs, recover the logical qudits. The authors determine when the bound holds, and when it fails, the maximum violation is tied to lengths of classical MDS codes. Apart from cited MDS lengths, the proofs are formalized in the Lean proof assistant. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize when the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound holds for linear stabilizer codes and its maximum violation, tied to classical MDS code lengths.

entry.title: Generalized tensor parallelism for training trillion-parameter LLMs at over 10 EFLOP/s
entry.summary: Generalized Tensor Parallelism: Powering Trillion-Parameter LLM Training at 10+ EFLOP/s arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper proposes generalized tensor parallelism (GTP), a framework that unifies data, tensor, sequence, context parallelism and fully sharded data parallelism as special cases for linear layers. It schedules parameter all-gathers per matrix multiplication rather than per Transformer block to balance communication hiding and memory use. The authors report 13.0 model EFLOP/s and 98% weak-scaling efficiency for an internal 2-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model on 12,288 GB300 GPUs. Throughput is reported as 1.05 to 1.55 times that of Megatron-FSDP and 1.27 to 1.31 times that of a tuned 3D-parallel recipe on 256 to 1,024 GPUs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors unify five parallelisms into generalized tensor parallelism, scheduling all-gathers per GEMM; the abstract reports throughput gains on a 2T MoE and 256–1,024 GPUs.

entry.title: HuluOPD: Merging Different Medical Specialist AI Models into One Small Model Using Unlabeled Prompts
entry.summary: HuluOPD: Unifying Heterogeneous Medical Specialists into One Lightweight Model with Unlabeled Prompts arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper presents HuluOPD, a distillation method that combines several medical specialist vision-language models, which may differ in architecture and tokenizer, into one lightweight model. It uses only unlabeled prompts, with no reference answers or specialists' training data, and the specialist matching each prompt's imaging modality supervises the lightweight model's response. Tested on five specialists covering ultrasound, pathology, optical coherence tomography, fundus photography, and dental imaging, a model with 10% of their combined parameters retains 94% of their question-answering performance, and one with 2% retains 89%. ★★★★ Notable: The authors distill heterogeneous medical specialist VLMs into one lightweight model using only unlabeled prompts, reporting 94% retained QA performance on 132k test items.

entry.title: Learning Agent States for Latent Action Modeling: Learning compact states that capture only an agent's own motion from unlabeled video
entry.summary: Learning Agent States for Latent Action Modeling arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper proposes Agent-State LAM, which jointly learns a compact agent-state representation and the latent actions that model its transitions from unlabeled video. To keep latents from encoding background and persistent agent appearance, it introduces spatially matched temporal discrimination (SMTD), which trains the state by matching frozen local visual features across spatial locations. Experiments on distracting control tasks and six real robot video datasets report improved action recovery, downstream control, and world-model prediction. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a compact agent-state representation with spatially matched temporal discrimination, and report experiments on distracting control tasks and six real robot datasets.

entry.title: Training language models on real audience behavior
entry.summary: Grounding Language Models in Revealed Audience Behavior arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper fine-tunes language models on records of what audiences actually clicked, liked, or watched, rather than on what people say they would do. On headline click prediction, an 8B model grounded in click data reaches 86.5% accuracy, while the same model asked directly is right about half the time. The authors argue the gap comes mainly from the training signal rather than model size or prompting, and report similar gains for short-video likes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors fine-tune language models on real audience clicks and likes rather than stated opinions, comparing against prompting across four behaviors, with code release promised.

entry.title: Reconstructing natural images from brain activity while monkeys freely view scenes
entry.summary: Reconstructing Natural Images from Brain Activity during Natural Vision arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents a framework for reconstructing natural images from neural activity recorded while primates freely move their eyes over a static scene. Recordings from five monkeys in the lateral geniculate nucleus and primary visual cortex are combined across eye movements, trials, and sessions to cover the full image. The authors start with a linear method using a 1/f prior and then scale up with a transformer and diffusion model, reporting state-of-the-art results across fMRI, EEG, MEG and electrophysiology. ★★★★ Notable: The authors reconstruct full natural scenes from free-viewing monkey LGN and V1 recordings using gaze tokens and diffusion, reporting state-of-the-art results across modalities.

entry.title: Trade-offs between queries and samples for revenue maximization
entry.summary: Query-Sample Tradeoffs for Revenue Maximization arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies revenue maximization against a single buyer whose value follows an unknown distribution. The learner can combine value samples, which reveal the buyer's full value, with pricing queries, which only reveal whether a fresh buyer accepts a chosen price. The authors give tight or almost tight bounds on how many extra pricing queries are needed as the sample budget shrinks, for monotone-hazard-rate, regular, quasi-monotone-hazard-rate, and quasi-regular distributions. For quasi-MHR distributions, additional samples reduce the query requirement by polynomial factors, while for MHR and regular distributions, a small fraction of samples still leaves the query cost close to the single-sample level. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize the full sample-query tradeoff for revenue maximization, giving tight bounds for MHR and regular families and removing a logarithmic factor.

entry.title: Can web agents still be detected? Testing bot defenses against coordinated evasion
entry.summary: Are Web Agents Still Detectable? Stress-Testing Bot Defenses with Coordinated Evasion arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper introduces DarkAgent, an autonomous web agent that hides automation traces using a modified Chromium browser and generative models producing human-like mouse and keyboard behavior. It reports an 89% page-access bypass rate on a third-party stealth benchmark, 12 percentage points above the strongest published baseline. The authors also present a benchmark measuring browser fingerprints, interaction behavior, and network activity, finding that only combining browser and behavioral changes evades all tested checks. The timing between actions is identified as a remaining signal for defenders. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine fingerprint, automation, and behavior evasion with a new keyboard timing model, reporting 89% bypass on a third-party stealth benchmark and a multi-channel detection benchmark.

entry.title: Generating Passive Macromodels Directly from Layouts Using Nested Port-Hamiltonian Learning
entry.summary: Learning in the Passive Space: End-to-End Muti-Order Port-Hamiltonian Macromodeling arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper presents an end-to-end method that generates multi-order port-Hamiltonian (pH) macromodels directly from physical layout graphs, for transient signal and power-integrity simulation of interconnects and power-delivery networks. A prefix-nested pH parameterization guarantees passivity and stability over continuous frequency by construction. The authors report that on 27k unseen test structures, the method reduces mean S-parameter error by 42% relative to established tools fitted to electromagnetic simulation data, and speeds up macromodel generation by 11,000 to 39,000 times. ★★★★ Notable: The authors embed a nested port-Hamiltonian parameterization in learning, reporting 42% lower S-parameter error on 27k unseen structures and zero passivity violations.

entry.title: How Geometry Shapes Generated Motion in Video Models
entry.summary: Motion Without State: Probing Dynamical Consistency and Conditioning Bias in Video Models arXiv · Oct 4, 2026The paper fixes a physical law and initial state, changing only the geometry in the first frame, and compares generated trajectories with simulator predictions. Across nine image-to-video models, geometry shapes motion (e.g., ball speed follows track undulations), but the evolution of state systematically departs from a fixed physical law. The study also finds text mainly controls destination and clip length mainly controls timing in the open-weight models tested.) ★★★★ Notable: Fixing the law and initial state and varying only first-frame geometry, the authors compare nine models with simulator predictions, reporting geometry is preserved yet state evolution systematically d

entry.title: Quantum sampling for gradient-based simulation optimization beyond classical minimax rates
entry.summary: Beyond Classical Minimax Rates: Quantum Sampling in Gradient-Based Simulation Optimization arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies gradient-based search for convex simulation optimization problems, where gradients are estimated from noisy outputs. The authors apply quantum mean estimation to paired finite differences, increasing estimation accuracy as perturbations shrink, which improves the convergence rate from the classical O(N^{-2/3}) to O(N^{-4/3}). They also give rates for coupled nearby evaluations and prove matching lower bounds showing these accuracy exponents are minimax optimal for fixed decision dimension. ★★★★ Notable: The authors apply quantum mean estimation to paired finite differences, improving the convergence exponent and reporting matching minimax lower bounds for simulation optimization.

entry.title: Coherent conversion between mesons and baryons in a cold-atom non-Abelian lattice gauge simulator
entry.summary: Coherent meson-baryon conversion in a cold-atom non-Abelian lattice gauge simulator arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper realizes a non-Abelian lattice gauge model with dynamical matter in an analog cold-atom simulator and observes its hadronic dynamics with site- and spin-resolved quantum gas microscopy. It uses two hyperfine states and site occupations of 87Rb atoms to encode both matter and gauge fields, and tailors resonant tunneling in a spin-dependent optical superlattice to implement a truncated one-dimensional SU(2) quantum link model. Slow mass ramps reveal coherent oscillations between mesons and baryon-antibaryon pairs, with the conversion efficiency characterized against mass, gauge coupling and net baryon density. ★★★★ Notable: The authors realize a non-Abelian lattice gauge model in cold atoms and report coherent meson-baryon oscillations observed with quantum gas microscopy.

entry.title: Neural decoder for logical Clifford circuits built from transversal gates
entry.summary: Neural Decoding of Logical Clifford Circuits with Transversal Gates arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents Duet, a neural decoder for logical Clifford circuits that use transversal gates, which builds in known gate structure and how logical outcomes propagate, learning only which errors occurred. On circuits with 2 to 4 blocks and up to 16 layers, Duet alone beats matching at every distance, and paired with the Tesseract search decoder it fails 44 times less often than LoMatching at distance 9. The method takes 2.4 to 121.7 microseconds per layer. ★★★★ Notable: The authors embed known error propagation and linear logical outcome flips into a neural decoder paired with Tesseract; the abstract reports much lower failure rates than matching and LoMatching on ra

entry.title: Spinal reflected entropy reveals logical magic
entry.summary: Spinal reflected entropy reveals logical magic arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper links quantum entanglement and quantum magic in the toric code. It introduces spinal reflected entropy, which connects the stabilizer Rényi entropy of the stored logical state to entanglement. The quantity obeys an area law with a topological correction, and the result extends to higher-genus surfaces and general two-dimensional topological stabilizer codes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors link logical magic to a geometric reflected-entropy quantity, give an analytic relation on the torus, and extend it to higher-genus surfaces and general topological stabilizer codes.

entry.title: Locality from Nonlocality: Relocalizing Symmetries and Gauging Lattice Dirac Fermions
entry.summary: Locality from Nonlocality: Symmetry Relocalization and Gauging of Lattice Dirac Fermions arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper shows that certain exact nonlocal compact symmetries of free lattice Dirac fermions can be made onsite through nonlocal canonical transformations while preserving enough Hamiltonian locality to allow gauging. It studies this symmetry relocalization in one, two, and three dimensions, relating gauge locality to lattice structure, topology, and anomalies. The work also covers bosonization, duality, and non-Abelian extensions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a nonlocal canonical transformation relocalizing compact symmetries in 1D, 2D, and 3D, with norm-resolvent bounds and no-go theorems.

entry.title: Meta-Amortized Cognitive Modeling: One Network for Fitting Many Cognitive Models
entry.summary: Meta-Amortized Cognitive Modeling arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper introduces CogFormerV2, a meta-amortized framework that lets researchers specify, revise, and fit cognitive models using a single neural network. Trained once in about a day on one GPU, it produces accurate, well-calibrated posteriors across more than 14.6 billion model configurations covering binary, multi-alternative, and continuous decisions. It can also fit empirical data from different behavioral tasks and extends to new models through continual learning and representation transfer. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend amortized inference to a single network spanning over 14.6 billion model configurations, reporting fits to empirical data and continual-learning extension.

entry.title: JECT: Fixing a Shortcut in Chest CT Self-Supervised Learning
entry.summary: JECT: Addressing the Context Shortcut in Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning for Chest CT arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper proposes JECT, a self-supervised pretraining method for chest CT scans. Standard masked prediction can ignore diagnostically important findings, such as small nodules, because they are hard to infer from surrounding anatomy, a failure the authors call the context shortcut. JECT uses the radiology report both as a condition for the predictor and as a target, where the encoder predicts masked anatomical report sections, within a hierarchical 3D encoder. Trained from scratch on 173k volumes, the authors report performance comparable to current CT foundation models on classification, retrieval and nodule malignancy, and to task-specific models on lung-cancer risk after fine-tuning. Code and pretrained weights are released. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use radiology reports both as predictor condition and as masked section-text target, addressing the context shortcut; ablations on 173k chest CT volumes compare against foundation models,

entry.title: Spec-Test Coverage Gap: Finding Overly Strict Tests in SWE-Bench-Style Benchmarks
entry.summary: Spec-Test Coverage Gap: Detecting Overspecified Tests in SWE-Bench-Style Benchmarks arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper examines coding-agent benchmarks such as SWE-bench Verified and SWE-bench Pro, whose tests can require details that the task never states. It defines a Spec-Test Coverage Gap (STCG) score from 1 to 4 and uses two LLM judges to flag overspecified tasks. The authors report that the judges correctly flagged 89% of human-identified overspecified tasks and wrongly flagged 4% of fine tasks. Flagged tasks were resolved far less often by top submissions, and relaxing the tests let 61% of failed patches on those tasks pass. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a spec-test coverage gap metric, detect overspecified tests with LLM judges, and report leaderboard changes on SWE-bench-style benchmarks.

entry.title: Using LLM Agents to Find Soundness Bugs in Safe Rust Bindings
entry.summary: Agentic Discovery of Soundness Bugs in Safe Rust Bindings arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies whether LLM agents can audit the safe interfaces of Rust crates that wrap unsafe code such as C or C++ libraries. The authors define a taxonomy of defects, including undefined behavior, divergences from the wrapped library, and incomplete unsafe contracts, and measure audits by a closed and an open model. They present Crustify, an agentic system built on these findings, which reported 83 findings across widely used crates and the Linux kernel's Rust abstractions, with 26 fixed by maintainers. ★★★★ Notable: The authors apply LLM agents to audit safe Rust bindings, reporting 225 undefined-behavior bugs across 16 crates and 11 more in the Linux kernel.

entry.title: HDMark: A Watermark That Proves Ownership of Hyperdimensional Computing Models
entry.summary: HDMark: Holographic Multi-Bit Model Watermarking for Intellectual Property Protection in Hyperdimensional Computing arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper presents HDMark, the first watermarking framework built for hyperdimensional computing (HDC) models, which embeds a multi-bit owner identity into trained class prototype hypervectors. A statistical test verifies ownership, and across four datasets and three learning rules accuracy stays essentially unchanged while a 64-bit identity is verified in 99.8% of trials. The authors also identify a dimension-permutation attack specific to HDC and counter it through encoder realignment, and an FPGA implementation shows no added hardware overhead. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose the first HDC-native model watermark embedding multi-bit identities; the abstract reports experiments on four datasets and an FPGA implementation, with impact mainly on HDC edge de

entry.title: Optimal square-root bound for online fair allocation of indivisible goods with known agent types
entry.summary: An Order-Optimal Square-Root Bound for Online Maximin Share Allocation with Known Types arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper studies allocating indivisible goods to agents who arrive online and reveal one of k known additive valuation types, receiving irrevocable bundles immediately. The authors give a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm, Single-or-Select, guaranteeing each agent about 1/√(2k) of their truncated proportional share, which dominates maximin share. They also tighten the upper bound to about √2/√k even for binary valuations, showing the optimal order is Θ(k^{-1/2}). Further exact results cover two arrivals, three arrivals with two types, and randomized policies. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report an order-optimal Θ(k^{-1/2}) deterministic MMS bound via a polynomial-time algorithm, with tight bounds for two and three arrivals.

entry.title: Tokenization and architecture jointly determine which components build features in time series transformers
entry.summary: Tokenization and Architecture Jointly Allocate Component Roles in Time Series Transformers arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper examines whether attention or the feed-forward network (FFN) in time series transformers constructs temporal features, and how tokenization such as patching affects this division. The authors propose a probing framework using 15 token-level diagnostic tasks to measure feature construction. Tested on 5 supervised models across 8 long-term forecasting benchmarks, they find that the constructing component is allocated by the interaction of tokenization and architecture rather than being fixed. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a probing framework measuring feature construction via linear decodability gains, and report that tokenization and architecture jointly determine the constructing component across

entry.title: PRETZEL: A Benchmark for Predicting Cyclic Peptide Structures
entry.summary: PRETZEL: A Benchmark for Cyclic Peptide Structure Prediction arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper introduces PRETZEL, a benchmark of 285 curated cyclic peptide-protein complexes spanning three cyclization chemistries, all released after the training cutoffs of the evaluated models. It tests AlphaFold3, Boltz-2, Protenix-v2, and HighFold3, with Protenix-v2 achieving the best median RMSD of 9.05 Å. The authors also find that chemical validity is weak, with at most 8.1% of predictions having fully valid inter-residue bonds, so pose accuracy alone is insufficient. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a unified cyclic peptide benchmark with chemical validity checks, evaluating four co-folding models on 285 complexes and reporting poor ring-closure validity despite pose accurac

entry.title: Harvesting Apple's Orchard: Security Analysis of On-Device CoreML Models
entry.summary: Harvesting Apple's Orchard: A Security Analysis of On-Device CoreML Models Across the Apple Ecosystem arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents a systematic security analysis of hundreds of on-device CoreML machine-learning models shipped across Apple's iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and tvOS platforms. The authors collected 1,137 artifacts and converted 155 previously opaque bundles into loadable form. They report findings including plaintext learned parameters, adversarial inputs that flip classifier outputs at high rates, and small weight edits that change model behavior without a runtime integrity check. Three reports sent to Apple were declined as not crossing a security boundary, so the findings are presented as robustness results. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report the first systematic security analysis of Apple's on-device CoreML models, with large-scale adversarial evaluations across 221 model paths.

entry.title: Constant-factor single-sample prophet inequality for subadditive valuations
entry.summary: A Constant-Factor Single-Sample Prophet Inequality for Subadditive Valuations arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies online combinatorial allocation where buyers have monotone subadditive valuations and each buyer provides one independent sample from an unknown distribution. The authors give a reduction that turns any offline algorithm achieving an α fraction of optimal welfare into an online algorithm achieving an α/120 fraction of the expected offline optimum. The guarantee holds for arbitrary arrival orders and extends to the Game of Googol model. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend single-sample prophet inequalities to monotone subadditive valuations, giving a reduction with a 1/120 constant factor for arbitrary arrival orders.

entry.title: Your bids are showing: re-identifying power plants in anonymized market data, with a differentially private alternative
entry.summary: Your bids are showing: re-identifying power plants in anonymized market data, and a differentially private alternative arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper tests PJM's practice of replacing generator names with codes in published offer data and finds that, when matched against public EIA and EPA records, about 25% of scorable units can be tied to their plant. It proposes a differentially private release of monthly noisy totals by fuel group and price bin, from which supply curves are derived. At epsilon=10 per unit-year, the market supply curve stays within 11% of the truth. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show plant identities can be re-identified from masked PJM-style offer data using ERCOT ground truth, and propose a zCDP-calibrated monthly noisy release for market supply curves.

entry.title: Medical image segmentation as a coding task: agents build and refine their own segmenters
entry.summary: Medical Image Segmentation Is Now Just Another Coding Task arXiv · Nov 24, 2026Researchers gave four off-the-shelf coding agents only a task description, labeled data, and a CPU, with no segmentation framework or pretrained weights. Within hours, the agents built segmenters for 13 tasks across four imaging modalities, with the best programs reaching 99% of the Dice score of a GPU-trained nnU-Net on nine 2D tasks. Agents improve by inspecting renderings of their own predictions, and gains grow further when they are told the true Dice score. The paper identifies a lack of reference-free quality estimation as the main bottleneck. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report coding agents building segmenters for 13 medical tasks without experts or pretrained weights, reaching 99% of nnU-Net's Dice on nine 2D tasks, and identify a reference-free quality

entry.title: What You See Is What You Certify: Certificates from Concepts for Unseen Part Combinations
entry.summary: What You See Is What You Certify: Concept-Based Certificates for Unseen Compositions arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper examines whether concept-based models can treat their predicted concepts as reliable certificates for decisions on unseen combinations of familiar parts. It finds that standard-trained models often certify wrong classes, partly due to cross-concept shortcuts. The authors propose OCVE, a design that reads each part from a local crop, which lowers certified risk on unseen FunnyBirds classes and also reduces risk on CUB and real traffic sign data. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose ontology-as-error-code certificate criteria and OCVE, reporting lower certified risk on unseen compositions across FunnyBirds, CUB, and traffic signs.

entry.title: What a Forecasting Leaderboard Can Establish: Resolution Reporting for Zero-Shot Time-Series Models
entry.summary: What a Forecasting Leaderboard Can Establish: Resolution Reporting for Zero-Shot Time-Series Models arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper argues that leaderboards used to compare zero-shot time-series forecasting models do not state how small a score difference they can detect. It defines this as a board's resolution and introduces Vernier, a tool that computes it from published per-dataset scores. Vernier also reports which entries cannot be separated from the leader and whether rankings change when unrelated submissions are added. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose board resolution, a tool computing it, and report that major leaderboards cannot separate neighbouring entries and reorder with submissions.

entry.title: Why Shared Networks Work Across Diffusion Noise Levels: Adjacency Matters
entry.summary: Noise-Level Adjacency in Diffusion Training arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper examines why diffusion models use one network across all noise levels and why this often beats separate networks for adjacent level pairs. The authors find the benefit comes from adjacency in the noise-level embedding rather than from the direction of that order. Experiments on a Gaussian mixture and CIFAR-10 show that reversing the embeddings leaves fitting error unchanged, while shuffling them increases it. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show that noise-level sharing benefits in diffusion training arise from adjacency rather than direction, with a fitting-error lower bound; experiments on a Gaussian mixture and CIFAR-10 ar

entry.title: Adapt, Label, Distill: Using Foundation-Model Supervision to Build Efficient Object Detectors
entry.summary: Adapt, Label, Distill: Foundation-Model Supervision for Efficient Object Detection arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper presents a pipeline that adapts the SAM3 foundation model using limited labeled target-domain data, generates pseudo-labels for unlabeled images, and trains compact YOLOv11 detectors with confidence-guided supervision. Experiments on six target domains and three student sizes show strong gains in some domains and limited or negative transfer in others. With YOLOv11m, the method improves over STAC-style self-training by up to 15.3 AP and reaches 51.6 AP on Garbage. The deployed student runs at 188 FPS on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, compared with 2.9 FPS for SAM3. ★★★★ Notable: The authors adapt SAM3 with few labels, distill its confidence-weighted pseudo-labels into YOLOv11 across six domains, and report up to 15.3 AP gains over STAC.

entry.title: Lit Up but Not Needed: Scoped Lesions Test Whether Multimodal MoE Models Depend on Their Experts
entry.summary: Lit Up but Not Needed: Scoped Lesions Show Where Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts Depend on Their Experts arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper argues that an expert activation map does not show which experts a model needs, so it tests this with lesion experiments on three mixture-of-experts vision-language models: Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B, Kimi-VL-A3B and Gemma-4-26B-A4B. Removing vision-exclusive experts costs no more than removing a random set of the same size. Limiting removal to image or text positions shows that image-side dependence is small in most models, while reading text in images is the one ability that needs image-position experts in every model. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use lesion experiments to test modality experts' necessity, reporting vision-exclusive experts are largely dispensable across three MoE vision-language models and multiple benchmarks, info

entry.title: Safe Autoformalization Using Entailment Graphs for Sufficiency and Necessity
entry.summary: Safe Autoformalization: Sufficiency and Necessity with Entailment Graphs arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper proposes a method for safely translating natural-language statements into logical formulas. It uses LLMs to generate candidate formulas, orders them by logical strength in an Entailment Graph, and finds sufficient and necessary frontiers that bracket the statement's meaning. On security-critical AWS properties, the method was safe in all 20 expert-adjudicated cases, and the proofs were machine-checked in Lean. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build entailment-graph sufficient and necessary frontiers with residuals for one-sided safe autoformalization, compare against majority-vote and USC baselines on AWS properties, and report

entry.title: Aftershock: Linux kernel bugs from yesterday becoming Android exploits tomorrow
entry.summary: Aftershock: Yesterday's Linux Kernel Bugs, Tomorrow's Android Exploits arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper examines how Android kernels receive upstream Linux fixes much later than conventional distributions. The authors built an automated pipeline that screens upstream patches, reproduces memory-safety vulnerabilities on Android targets, and uses an LLM agent to build local privilege escalation exploits from an untrusted app. From 152 candidate CVEs reported over 33 months, they reproduced 38 vulnerabilities and generated 17 independently verified exploits under production defenses. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report an LLM-agent pipeline that builds Android kernel n-day privilege escalation exploits from upstream patches, tested on Pixel 9 and Pixel 10 devices.

entry.title: Reproducible social structures emerging from free interaction among LLM agents
entry.summary: Reproducible Social Structure Emerges From Free-Form Interaction Among LLM Agents arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper introduces a repeatable, goal-free multi-agent framework in which fifty persona-conditioned agents with persistent memory choose whether, with whom, and how to communicate across three social platforms. Running the same world ten times from identical starting conditions for 700 hours, the authors find that most network- and agent-level measures are stable across repetitions, with communication narrowing into sparse sustained dyads. They report that alignment and extremity of emotions and traits expressed at first contact predict later sustained dyads better than static personality similarity. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a repeatable goal-free LLM agent society and report stable social structure and predictable dyads across ten repeated worlds.

entry.title: Tempering and few-shot calibration make pathology AI biomarkers more consistent across slide scanners
entry.summary: Tempering and few-shot calibration of pathology foundation models improve digital biomarker reproducibility across slide scanners arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper presents a fine-tuning method called tempering for pathology foundation models, aiming to reduce their dependence on scanner-specific image signatures. The method is tested on head-and-neck cancer HPV prediction, colorectal cancer MSI identification, prostate cancer grading and breast cancer phenotyping. The authors report that cross-scanner prediction differences fell by 67.5% for HPV and 69.3% for MSI, and prostate grade agreement across scanners rose from 42.5% to 92.7%. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a tempering fine-tuning method that reduces scanner dependence, reporting large cross-scanner gains on HPV, MSI, prostate, and breast tasks.

entry.title: Hi3R-VLA: A 3D robot model linking vision, language, and actions
entry.summary: Hi3R-VLA: Grounding Semantics and Actions in 3D arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper introduces Hi3R-VLA, a 3D policy for robotic manipulation that links vision, language, and actions to explicit 3D geometry. It adds spatially aligned visual features and language conditioning to point clouds, and uses 3D-RoPE enhanced action-to-point attention to model relationships between action targets and observed points. With fewer than 250M trainable parameters, it achieves state-of-the-art results on RoboCasa, RLBench, RoboTwin2, DexJoCo and DexSuite, and real-robot tests confirm its effectiveness. The model, code and dataset are publicly released. ★★★★ Notable: The authors fuse vision and language features into point clouds, anchor actions in 3D with 3D-RoPE attention, and report results on several benchmarks and real robots.

entry.title: Optimal signaling mechanisms for one-round matching markets
entry.summary: Optimal Signaling Mechanisms for One-round Matching Markets arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies signaling mechanisms in a one-round matching market with n applicants and n firms, where applicants signal interest in firms to improve matching outcomes. It considers a richer signal space than prior work and analyzes both deterministic and randomized mechanisms. In the limit as k grows, the optimal deterministic mechanism yields about 75.45% of applicants receiving offers, and the optimal randomized mechanism yields about 78.20%. ★★★★ Notable: The authors consider richer signal spaces and randomized signaling mechanisms, reporting optimal offer rates of about 75.45% deterministic and 78.20% randomized as k grows.

entry.title: Reading Between the Layers: Where Model Representation Quality Lies and What Geometry Shows
entry.summary: Reading Between the Layers: Where Representation Quality Lives, and What Geometry Reveals arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper is a large-scale empirical study of how representation quality varies across layers in 25 pretrained text models from four architectural families and four pretraining strategies, tested on 13 datasets. It finds that the layer that performs best for probing depends systematically on pretraining strategy and architecture. The authors propose the Stable Geometry Index (SGI), a label-free, closed-form selector that improves over using the last layer and recovers 40% of the gap to the oracle choice. ★★★★ Notable: The authors map peak probing layers by pretraining strategy and architecture, and propose SGI, a label-free, coefficient-free layer selector; they report Hit@3 rising from 0.39 to 0.52 across 383 eval

entry.title: CHORD: A Latent-Space Learning Method for Constrained Stellarator Design
entry.summary: CHORD: Learning Latent Spaces for Constrained Stellarator Design arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper introduces CHORD, a conditional variational autoencoder that penalizes constraint violations along decoded latent interpolation paths during training and uses self-consistent inference to align conditioning with the decoded design's predicted metrics. In interpolation between distinct stellarator geometry families, CHORD achieved up to 81% simulator-validated mid-segment feasibility, versus 50% for an unregularized model and 28% for direct boundary-parameter interpolation. The authors also report denser Pareto-front coverage on the ConStellaration benchmark and release code and over 600k designs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors penalize constraint violations along decoded latent interpolants and report 81% simulator-validated mid-segment feasibility on stellarator interpolation, with ablations.

entry.title: Pearl: TEE-enabled fair transaction ordering with fewer replicas
entry.summary: Pearl: TEE-Enabled Fair Ordering with Minimal Replication arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies fair transaction ordering in blockchain consensus and how trusted execution environments (TEEs) can reduce the number of replicas needed. It proves that, in partially synchronous networks, ordering linearizability and γ-batch-order fairness cannot be achieved with 2f+1 replicas even when TEEs are used, because Byzantine replicas can manipulate submission timing. Under a synchronous network assumption, the authors propose two mechanisms that guarantee these properties with fewer replicas. They integrate these mechanisms into a synchronous lane-based consensus algorithm that outperforms representative baselines while using fewer replicas. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine TEEs with fair ordering, prove an impossibility for 2f+1 replicas and two synchronous constructions, integrating them into a consensus protocol.

entry.title: A dataset of similar medical image pairs from linked case reports for image retrieval
entry.summary: A dataset of clinically similar image pairs from citation-linked case reports for medical image retrieval arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The authors built PMC-PaIR, a dataset of 86,144 pairs of clinically similar medical images drawn from 56,013 open-access PubMed Central case reports, which often describe rare or challenging presentations. They followed citations linking similar patients and used large language models to answer hierarchical questions about modality, diagnosis and findings before matching images by caption. Experts rated the pairs as highly accurate, and the question-guided method found twice as many correct pairs as direct matching. Fine-tuning BiomedCLIP on the dataset improved retrieval across all tested categories, and the dataset and pipeline are released for extension. ★★★★ Notable: The authors build a large dataset of clinically similar image pairs by following case report citations and hierarchical LLM questions, reporting expert review and BiomedCLIP retrieval gains.

entry.title: A foundation model combining tissue morphology and protein profiling for cancer
entry.summary: A multimodal foundation model for tissue proteomics and morphology in cancer arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper presents VirTues-M2, a vision transformer-based multimodal foundation model that jointly learns from H&E histopathology and multiplex spatial proteomics. By encoding marker identity during pretraining, it handles missing modalities and variable marker panels, supporting tasks such as tissue phenotyping, cell segmentation, and virtual staining. In 1,053 treatment-naive non-small-cell lung cancer patients, it identified high-risk and low-risk tissue signatures that stratified overall survival in both discovery and independent validation cohorts, outperforming current stratification methods. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors jointly learn H&E and spatial proteomics in one vision transformer that encodes marker identity, and report improved overall-survival stratification over existing schemes in 1,053 NSCLC pa

entry.title: When successful teamwork becomes an attack route: poisoning shared memory from within a multi-agent system
entry.summary: When Successful Collaboration Becomes an Attack Surface: Insider Memory Poisoning in Multi-Agent Systems arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper proposes MIMPA (Multi-Agent Insider Memory Poisoning Attack), which exploits shared memory that multi-agent systems use to store successful collaboration records. A malicious agent, using only normal participation privileges, embeds a target-specific payload during an earlier task so it is kept as successful team experience. When this record is retrieved for a later task, it steers benign agents toward a designated wrong answer. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show shared collaboration memory can become a persistent insider attack channel, reporting gains over prior attacks on three benchmarks and two LLM backbones.

entry.title: MOZAIC: A Paired Audio-Video Deepfake Benchmark That Separates Fake Video from Fake Audio
entry.summary: MOZAIC: An Audio-Video Deepfake Benchmark for Telling What Is Fake arXiv · Nov 22, 2026The paper introduces MOZAIC, a paired benchmark of 137,745 audio-video clips with four-way labels covering all combinations of real or fake video and audio. It includes four tasks: authenticity, manipulation type, identity verification, and explanation. The authors evaluate 12 audio-video multimodal LLMs and train four detectors to measure how much each modality contributes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce paired four-way audio-video deepfake benchmark, evaluating 12 MLLMs and trained detectors on 137,745 clips.

entry.title: Static detection of exactly-once violations in payment pipelines
entry.summary: The Defect Is in the Arithmetic Between the Files: Static Detection of Exactly-Once Violations in Payment Pipelines arXiv · Nov 21, 2026The paper argues that whether a streaming payment pipeline double-charges a customer after a restart depends on comparing how long a provider remembers an idempotency key with how stale a record can be when reprocessed, and these figures are scattered across separate files. The authors present a checker that gathers these facts and derives their relations, and a synthesiser that turns 335 of 515 findings into runnable replay scenarios. In live tests against a real Kafka broker with real process kills, all 16 selected witnesses reproduced their predicted outcomes, with 245 findings producing two charges. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors detect exactly-once violations by statically comparing idempotency-key lifetime with record staleness across files, reporting 16 live witnesses reproduced on real Kafka with process kills.

entry.title: Greedy Byte-Pair Encoding Reaches At Least 0.361 of Optimal Compression
entry.summary: Greedy BPE with Replacement Counts Achieves the Tight Approximation Ratio (1-e⁻²)/2 arXiv · Nov 6, 2026Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) builds a tokeniser by repeatedly merging the most frequent adjacent pair of symbols, measuring its usefulness by the total string-length reduction from k merges. It was previously known that this greedy rule achieves at least one third of the optimal reduction. The paper proves that it always achieves at least 0.361 of the optimal reduction, for every string, budget, and tie-breaking rule, improving the one-third bound. ★★★★ Notable: The authors improve the greedy BPE compression lower bound from one third to 0.361, give a proof, and explain why one third was a barrier.

entry.title: Kleptographic attacks on post-quantum crypto that account for key representation
entry.summary: Representation-Aware Kleptographic Attacks on Post-Quantum Cryptography IACR ePrint · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies hidden backdoors in post-quantum cryptography implementations introduced through Algorithm Substitution Attacks, focusing on how public keys are represented. It distinguishes seed-compressed from expanded-key interfaces and presents the first key-generation backdoor targeting HQC, which uses structural similarities with BIKE decoding so that a party holding the BIKE trapdoor can recover the randomness behind the victim's HQC secret state. The paper also contrasts this with ML-DSA and analyzes remaining seed-level attack surfaces. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present the first kleptographic key-generation backdoor for HQC, using BIKE-form carriers and a conditional indistinguishability proof, plus a proof-of-concept implementation.

entry.title: A paper showing two messages suffice for quantum interactive proof systems
entry.summary: Two messages suffice for quantum interactive proof systems arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies how many message rounds quantum interactive proof systems need. The authors show that any quantum interactive proof system can be parallelized to two messages, where the verifier sends halves of EPR pairs as quantum public coins and then uses only stoquastic verification after the prover responds. This fully characterizes two-message quantum interactive proof systems, which are shown to equal PSPACE. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that any quantum interactive proof compresses to two messages and, via PSPACE-hardness of CIUniform, fully characterize two-message systems.

entry.title: Computational complexity of concurrent stochastic games: exact values and approximation
entry.summary: The Computational Complexity of Concurrent Stochastic Games: Exact Value and Approximation arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies two-player zero-sum concurrent stochastic games on a finite state space played over infinitely many stages, with limit-average objectives for Player 1. It addresses two problems: approximating game values within an arbitrary additive error, and exactly deciding whether a state's value meets a given threshold. The authors show the approximation problem is in TFNP, with its gap version in NP ∩ coNP. They also show the exact problem lies in both the existential and universal theories of the reals and is PosSLP-hard. ★★★★ Notable: The paper studies limit-average values of two-player zero-sum concurrent stochastic games; the authors show the approximation problem lies in TFNP and its gap problem in NP∩coNP, and place the exact p

entry.title: Quantum Subentropy: Subadditivity and Sharp Bounds on Discrimination Error
entry.summary: Quantum Subentropy: Subadditivity and Sharp Bounds on Discrimination Error arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies quantum subentropy, which gives a tight spectral lower bound on the accessible information of pure-state ensembles. The authors prove subadditivity for arbitrary finite-dimensional bipartite states and derive a sharp relation between conditional subentropy and the minimum discrimination error. They also determine the optimal Lipschitz constant in trace distance for conditional subentropy on classical-quantum states, and show that strong subadditivity fails for quantum states while holding for classical distributions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove subadditivity of subentropy for finite-dimensional bipartite states and a sharp relation between conditional subentropy and minimum discrimination error. They report a counterexample

entry.title: Super-multiplicativity of a noncommutative minimum and its use in quantum privacy and hypothesis testing
entry.summary: Super-Multiplicativity of the Noncommutative Minimum and Applications to Quantum Privacy and Hypothesis Testing arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper studies the hockey-stick divergence, a measure of distinguishability in quantum information theory, on tensor-product states. It proves that a noncommutative minimum of positive semidefinite operators is super-multiplicative, which yields a sub-additivity property of the divergence on product states. The results are applied to quantum differential privacy composition and to symmetric binary quantum hypothesis testing, including the exact prefactor of the quantum Chernoff bound. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove super-multiplicativity of the noncommutative minimum, deduce sub-additivity of the hockey-stick divergence with applications to quantum privacy and hypothesis testing, and determine

entry.title: Relative Integrity and Robustness for Prompt Injection and Enclave-Partitioned Programs
entry.summary: Relativising Integrity and Robustness: Prompt Injection and Partitioned Enclaves arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper introduces relative integrity (RI) and relative robustness (RR), security properties that compare a system under attack with a reference system. RI requires every behaviour under attacker influence to be one the reference can exhibit, and RR requires the same runs to reproduce both leaks and effects. The properties are applied to LLM agents under prompt injection and to C programs partitioned across SGX or TrustZone enclaves. The work is mechanised in Isabelle/HOL, with enclave code verified in C using AutoCorres2. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose relative integrity (RI) and relative robustness (RR), which they say is strictly stronger than RS and RI combined, and give proof and disproof methods for prompt injection and encl

entry.title: Automatically discovering simple formula-based inventory ordering rules with AI
entry.summary: Agentic Discovery of Simple Symbolic Inventory Policies arXiv · Nov 22, 2026The paper presents an agentic system in which large language models revise symbolic policy structures while a numerical engine fits parameters and evaluates each inventory policy. Across 15,600 instances spanning 50 demand distributions, the discovered templates improve aggregate empirical performance over evaluated simple operational formula benchmarks and are competitive with more elaborate policies. For a lost-sales system with a three-period lead time, the authors prove that under specified conditions a capped dual-shortfall specialization of a discovered policy strictly outperforms every policy in the considered capped base-stock class. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use LLM-driven symbolic evolution to discover simple inventory policies, test them on 15,600 instances, and report a proof that under stated demand and cost conditions a capped dual-shortf

entry.title: Lowering the Bar for Everyone: Hidden Validation-Seeking Goals in Empathetic RL
entry.summary: Lowering the Bar for Everyone: Hidden Validation-Seeking Goals in Empathetic RL arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies what a reinforcement learning policy learns when some users privately want validation. Using empathetic RL with LLM-simulated users, the authors vary only the share of validation-seeking users from 0 to 50% and evaluate on 1,000 Reddit AITA posts. The policy lowers its threshold for endorsement, endorsing at-fault posters more as that share rises. Explicitly asking to be told if one is wrong does not prevent this shift. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report that validation-seeking users shift RL policy thresholds rather than targeting, measured via controlled user-share experiments on 1,000 AITA posts and signal-detection analysis.

entry.title: RigidAnchor: Drone-to-satellite location and heading estimation via iterative planar rigid alignment
entry.summary: RigidAnchor: Cross-View Geo-Localization for UAV via Iterative Planar Rigid Alignment arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper proposes RigidAnchor, a method for estimating a drone's absolute position and heading without GNSS by matching its aerial image to satellite imagery. It treats the problem as solving a planar rigid transform (2D translation plus in-plane rotation) between the two images, using iterative refinement rather than tile retrieval. On Bearing-UAV-90K, cross-view mean position error is 78.6% lower and heading error is 69.7% lower than Bearing-UAV. ★★★★ Notable: The authors reformulate UAV-satellite geo-localization as iterative planar rigid transform estimation, jointly recovering position and heading; reported errors on Bearing-UAV-90K drop substantially.

entry.title: CivicBench: Robustly Detecting AI-Generated Political Videos
entry.summary: CivicBench: Robust Detection of AI-Generated Political Video arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper introduces CivicBench, a benchmark of 10,800 generated videos of invented politicians from eight open generators and 2,632 public-domain or openly licensed real clips, with attacks applied to both. It shows that published detectors reach at most 0.781 AUC and are easily fooled by tiny pixel-level changes. The authors propose Tau-Anchor, a fine-tuned encoder trained on attacked clips with a margin term, which reaches 0.941 AUC on the benchmark. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a political-video forgery benchmark with attacks and Tau-Anchor, a margin-based fine-tuning method; they report AUC .941 and higher detection under attack.

entry.title: A paper advancing the theory of approximate quantum measurements and recovery operations
entry.summary: Advancing the Theory of Pretty Good Quantum Operations arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper addresses the difficulty of finding optimal quantum measurements or recovery maps. It unifies pretty good measurements and Petz maps within a semidefinite programming framework with a tunable power, extending them to broader quantum tasks. For powers between one and three, it proves a stronger performance bound than the Barnum-Knill bound, which peaks at quadratic power. For structured channels such as stabilizer codes under Pauli noise, large powers make recovery approach a maximum likelihood decoder for maximally mixed inputs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors unify pretty good measurements and Petz maps in a tunable-power SDP framework and report a stronger bound than Barnum-Knill for powers from one to three.

entry.title: Cutting RSA-2048 factoring Toffoli counts below one billion using LLM-driven verifiable quantum compilation
entry.summary: Reducing RSA-2048 Factoring Resources Below One Billion Toffolis via LLM-Driven Verifiable Quantum Compilation arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies quantum circuits that use Shor's algorithm to factor 2048-bit RSA integers, redesigning an approximate residue number system pipeline with large language model-driven search. The authors build a deterministic compiler that produces a Pareto frontier of RSA-2048 circuits and analytically bound rare overflow probabilities. They verify elementary gate sequences across the RNS primes on representative circuits. Against Gidney's 2025 baseline under matched adder accounting, the paper reports a 70.1% reduction in minimum qubit-Toffoli product and up to 78.6% fewer expected factoring Toffolis, bringing RSA-2048 factoring below one billion Toffolis. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use LLM-driven search to redesign an RNS pipeline, reporting RSA-2048 factoring below one billion Toffolis versus Gidney's 2025 baseline.

entry.title: Linear entanglement suffices for f-routing: a quantum communication result
entry.summary: Linear entanglement suffices for f-routing arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies f-routing, a task in which Alice and Bob share a pre-prepared quantum state and each send one simultaneous message, after which the party chosen by a Boolean function f(x,y) recovers an unknown qubit. The authors show that 2n+2 shared EPR pairs suffice for every function f, improving the previous best bound for all functions, which was 2^{O(√(n log n))} qubits. The new strategy shifts the cost from the shared state to the messages, with Alice sending 2^{n+1}+1 qubits and Bob sending only classical bits. The result is formalized in Lean. ★★★★ Notable: The authors reduce the all-function entanglement upper bound from 2^O(√(n log n)) to 2n+2 EPR pairs, with the result formalized in Lean.

entry.title: Exponential gains in probing quantum systems by adding a single extra qubit
entry.summary: Exponential advantage in quantum observation with one extra qubit arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper proposes an algorithm that adds one extra qubit to a quantum machine to probe quantum many-body dynamics. The qubit coherently interferes dynamical trajectories, allowing exponentially many multi-time correlators to be estimated with exponentially fewer evolutions than ancilla-free schemes. Numerical experiments on a many-body system show higher-order probe signals predicted with orders-of-magnitude fewer experimental runs than previous methods. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose using one extra qubit to interfere trajectories, exponentially reducing runs, and report a proof of optimality plus numerical demonstration.

entry.title: Measuring superposition using quantum coherence via stochastic orthogonalization
entry.summary: Quantifying superposition via coherence by stochastic orthogonalization arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper proposes a way to measure how much a state is a superposition of nonorthogonal reference states, using quantum coherence. The authors show that orthogonalization can be realized as a measurement that maps each reference state onto a basis vector multiple, and define a state's degree of superposition from the largest average coherence such measurements extract. The paper also examines when one superposition can be converted into another with certainty. ★★★★ Notable: The authors define superposition degree via stochastic orthogonalization, turning any coherence measure into a superposition measure, and report a tight bound for interference terms.

entry.title: Universal stabilizer correlations in chaotic eigenstates
entry.summary: Universal stabilizer correlations in chaotic eigenstates arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies the stabilizer correlation, defined as the difference between the Rényi-2 mutual information and the mutual stabilizer Rényi entropy, which captures structure in quantum states beyond entanglement and nonstabilizerness. For chaotic eigenstates, the authors show that this correlation approaches a universal constant determined only by symmetries. The value is derived analytically from random-state ensembles for different symmetry classes and confirmed by exact calculations on a chaotic mixed-field Ising chain. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a universal stabilizer correlation constant for chaotic eigenstates, derived analytically from random-state ensembles and checked on a mixed-field Ising chain.

entry.title: Joint measurements and state updates in quantum field theory, tested with a Bell inequality
entry.summary: For whom the Bell tolls: joint measurements and state updates in quantum field theory arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper studies state update rules in the Fewster-Verch measurement framework for quantum field theory and their behaviour in Bell tests. For observables of the form A(f_i)*A(f_i), it derives the joint moment generating functional and a unique joint probability distribution. As an application, it builds a Bell test model using a coupled Proca-scalar model for polarization measurements and shows that this model can violate the CHSH inequality. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive joint moment generating functionals for commuting observables in the Fewster-Verch framework and build a QFT Bell test model reported to violate CHSH.
